item.title: 'What did I do wrong?': Ex-India star reveals how being dropped from team pushed him into depression
item.description: NEW DELHI: Being dropped from the Indian team was one of the toughest phases of Amit Mishra's cricket career. The former India leg-spinner has revealed that he battled depression for 18 months because he could not understand why he was not getting chances to play for the country. Mishra made his international debut in 2003. However, he soon found himself out of the Indian team. He was also not picked for some domestic tournaments. Despite continuing to play cricket, he kept wondering why he was being left out. Speaking to former India batter Aakash Chopra, Mishra opened up about how the setback affected him. “I went into depression for a year and a half. I kept thinking about what my mistake was. I was playing everywhere, but the only question in my mind was that, ‘what did I do wrong?’" Mishra said. A selector's advice helped Amit Mishra Mishra was also left out of the Duleep Trophy and the India A zonal setup. He struggled to understand why he was not getting opportunities until a selector spoke to him about his performances. “Then a selector told me that I was not performing. I sat down and thought, and I understood that I was thinking of playing for India itself but not performing in domestic cricket," he recalled. The selector's words made Mishra think about his approach. He realised that he was thinking too much about returning to the Indian team and not focusing enough on performing in domestic cricket. Mishra returned to domestic circuit, worked on his game, and his performances eventually helped him return to the Indian team in 2008, almost five years after his debut. He went on to play 22 Tests, 36 ODIs and 10 T20Is for India. He claimed taking 156 wickets across the three formats.

item.title: Ballon d'Or Feminin 2026 Power Rankings: Alexia Putellas on course to end Aitana Bonmati's three-year dominance of the Women's Golden Ball
item.description: Women's Ballon d'Or GFX - Getty/GOAL The Barcelona midfielder has won each of the last three prizes - but the 2026 accolade will go to someone else at Monday's ceremony in London after Bonmati's injury-hit campaign Aitana Bonmati has won each of the last three Ballons d'Or Feminin - but the accolade will go to someone else in 2026. Will it be two-time winner and fellow Barcelona star Alexia Putellas who reasserts herself as the best player in the women's game? Or could there be a new name on the honour roll when the Golden Ball is handed out in London on Monday? Unfortunately, Bonmati suffered a fractured fibula last November, one which required surgery and kept her on the sidelines until she made her return in May. She was still able to play her part as the Catalans won a quadruple, beating Lyon in the Champions League final , but not one big enough to even be nominated for a fourth Ballon d'Or. Adding to the intrigue is the fact that this was not a World Cup year in women's football, with the Africa Cup of Nations, won by Cameroon back in August , also not counting towards the voting for the 2026 Ballon d'Or Feminin. As such, it is performances for club in the 2025-26 season that will largely decide the ranking for this award, with the exception of those who participated in the Asian Cup, won by Japan , back in March. So, who are the front-runners for the 2026 award? GOAL runs through the likeliest winners of the Golden Ball ahead of the much-anticipated ceremony... Cata Coll (Barcelona) Cata Coll (Barcelona) In 2025-26: 23 clean sheets. Won UEFA Nations League, Champions League, Liga F, Supercopa de Espanam & Copa de la Reina. There are some games in which Cata Coll, as the goalkeeper in this dominant Barcelona team, doesn't have much to do. However, that just makes the instances where she is called into action all the more impressive. This year's Champions League final was a great example of as much . The final scoreline, which read 4-0 to Barca, might suggest that the Catalans had an easy time defeating Lyon to win a fourth European crown, but that is not true. Coll had to be on her A-game in the encounter, making four impressive saves to keep her side ahead before two late Salma Paralluelo goals put the gloss on the final result. That was one of 23 clean sheets Coll kept during an impressive 2025-26 season for Barca and Spain, in which she helped both teams enjoy fantastic success. Her contributions might sometimes be overlooked, but that Champions League final display should have served as a reminder of their importance and earn her some respect after her first-ever Ballon d'Or nomination. Mariona Caldentey (Arsenal) Mariona Caldentey (Arsenal) In 2025-26: Seven goals, five assists. Won UEFA Nations League & FIFA Women's Champions Cup. After finishing second in the Ballon d'Or voting last year , it's much less likely that Mariona Caldentey will clinch the Golden Ball this time around. The Spain international was certainly influential again

Will it be two-time winner and fellow Barcelona star Alexia Putellas who reasserts herself as the best player in the women's game? Or could there be a new name on the honour roll when the Golden Ball is handed out in London on Monday? Unfortunately, Bonmati suffered a fractured fibula last November, one which required surgery and kept her on the sidelines until she made her return in May. She was still able to play her part as the Catalans won a quadruple, beating Lyon in the Champions League final , but not one big enough to even be nominated for a fourth Ballon d'Or. Adding to the intrigue is the fact that this was not a World Cup year in women's football, with the Africa Cup of Nations, won by Cameroon back in August , also not counting towards the voting for the 2026 Ballon d'Or Feminin. As such, it is performances for club in the 2025-26 season that will largely decide the ranking for this award, with the exception of those who participated in the Asian Cup, won by Japan , back in March. So, who are the front-runners for the 2026 award? GOAL runs through the likeliest winners of the Golden Ball ahead of the much-anticipated ceremony... Cata Coll (Barcelona) Cata Coll (Barcelona) In 2025-26: 23 clean sheets. Won UEFA Nations League, Champions League, Liga F, Supercopa de Espanam & Copa de la Reina. There are some games in which Cata Coll, as the goalkeeper in this dominant Barcelona team, doesn't have much to do. However, that just makes the instances where she is called into action all the more impressive. This year's Champions League final was a great example of as much . The final scoreline, which read 4-0 to Barca, might suggest that the Catalans had an easy time defeating Lyon to win a fourth European crown, but that is not true. Coll had to be on her A-game in the encounter, making four impressive saves to keep her side ahead before two late Salma Paralluelo goals put the gloss on the final result. That was one of 23 clean sheets Coll kept during an impressive 2025-26 season for Barca and Spain, in which she helped both teams enjoy fantastic success. Her contributions might sometimes be overlooked, but that Champions League final display should have served as a reminder of their importance and earn her some respect after her first-ever Ballon d'Or nomination. Mariona Caldentey (Arsenal) Mariona Caldentey (Arsenal) In 2025-26: Seven goals, five assists. Won UEFA Nations League & FIFA Women's Champions Cup. After finishing second in the Ballon d'Or voting last year , it's much less likely that Mariona Caldentey will clinch the Golden Ball this time around. The Spain international was certainly influential again for Arsenal, helping them win the inaugural FIFA Women's Champions Cup , but Caldentey's attacking numbers were down on last year, both domestically and in the Champions League, due to the deeper role she was asked to play more consistently at club level. That is likely to have an impact on her chances, as will the fact that she also struggled to make her mark in the latter stages of the Gunners' European title defence, which was ended by Lyon at the semi-final stage . Expect last year's runner-up to still get votes, though. Vivianne Miedema (Manchester City) Vivianne Miedema (Manchester City) In 2025-26: 14 goals, five assists. Won Women's Super League & FA Cup. An unfortunate spell of injuries mean it's been a while since Vivianne Miedema was last nominated for the Ballon d'Or, with her absent from the final list since finishing 11th in 2022. But the Dutchwoman is widely regarded as one of the best players on the planet and, last season, she reminded everyone just why she recorded back-to-back top-five finishes in the Ballon d'Or voting in the two awards that preceded 2022, by playing a key role in a campaign that delivered Manchester City's first Women's Super League title in 10 years . Only two players scored more goals in the English top-flight last season than Miedema, who also ranked third for assists and second for combined direct goal contributions. City's lack of European football will hurt her case for matching some of the higher-ranked finishes she's had in the Ballon d'Or before, but the forward still earned herself a nomination after her first injury-free season for a while, with her goal-scoring return in the FA Cup final only enhancing her chances. Claudia Pina (Barcelona) Claudia Pina (Barcelona) In 2025-26: 32 goals, nine assists. Won UEFA Nations League, Champions League, Liga F, Supercopa de Espana & Copa de la Reina. Claudia Pina had a brilliant 2025-26 season. She won the Golden Boot in Liga F and was one of the most prolific forwards on the continent all season, to the benefit of both Spain, whom she helped win the Nations League, and Barca, who won the quadruple. However, she endured a little dip in that productivity during the second half of the season, failing to take advantage of the games on the big stage that Barca had. No goals, no assists and no headline-grabbing moments in the Champions League knockout stages, nor in the the Liga F Clasico with Real Madrid, means she sits lower down this ranking - though she did score in the Copa de la Reina final. Temwa Chawinga (Kansas City Current) Temwa Chawinga (Kansas City Current) In 2025-26: 18 goals, four assists. Won NWSL Shield & Golden Boot. It's always difficult to know how NWSL stars will be regarded in the Ballon d'Or voting as the league's schedule does not align with the award's parameters in terms of dates and cut-off points. Last year, there were just three NWSL stars nominated, and the presence of both Marta and Esther Gonzalez was more down to their major tournament exploits at international level. Temwa Chawinga's nomination, however, was rooted in her outstanding NWSL form. In the 2024 season, for which the final few months were relevant for the Ballon d'Or, Chawinga won the Golden Boot and Most Valuable Player awards. In the 2025 season, she once again collected both accolades while also helping the Kansas City Current win the NWSL Shield, and she's been electric in the 2026 campaign, too. As such, the forward should be respected again in the Ballon d'Or ranking, even if her incredible exploits for Malawi on their Women's Africa Cup of Nations debut do not fall into the period considered for voting. Yui Hasegawa (Manchester City) Yui Hasegawa (Manchester City) In 2025-26: Six goals, five assists. Won Asian Cup, Women's Super League & FA Cup. Nominated in 2023 and 2024, Yui Hasegawa is on the longlist again in 2026 after she was the heartbeat of a Man City team which took the WSL by storm last season. Playing in a brilliant double-pivot midfield with England youngster Laura Blindkilde Brown or United States international Sam Coffey, Hasegawa was given more license to get forward, which resulted in more goal contributions that will only aid her cause. That Hasegawa was a key player in Japan's Asian Cup triumph adds to her credentials in a big way, putting another trophy on her resumé alongside the WSL title that City claimed rather comfortably and the FA Cup triumph that came via a 4-0 win over Brighton . Klara Buhl (Bayern Munich) Klara Buhl (Bayern Munich) In 2025-26: 10 goals, 22 assists. Won Bundesliga, DFB-Supercup & DFB-Pokal. Players in Germany can be overlooked in the voting for this award, but Klara Buhl's incredible numbers cut through in 2025 and did so again in 2026 after another excellent season. The flying winger matched her goals and surpassed her assists in the Bundesliga from the 2024-25 campaign, with her Champions League numbers also soaring thanks to a remarkable eight assis

item.title: 'I want to accept it': Harmanpreet Kaur embraces life beyond captaincy, says cricket continues to give her happiness
item.description: Harmanpreet Kaur wants to keep things simple and let her batting do the talking. The India batter, who struck a magnificent 126 off 121 balls against Zimbabwe in the second ODI in Vadodara on Sunday, said she was focused on enjoying her cricket and accepting reality as she navigates a new phase in her career. Harmanpreet's century, which included 15 boundaries, helped India recover from an early setback and post a formidable 328/6. She shared a 153-run fifth-wicket partnership with Deepti Sharma, who remained unbeaten on 106, as India went on to register a commanding 121-run victory and take an unassailable 2-0 lead in the three-match series. Speaking after being named Player of the Match, Harmanpreet reiterated that enjoying her batting remained her priority, regardless of the circumstances surrounding her career. “I'm somebody who always likes to live life close to reality, and this is the reality now, and I just want to accept it in whatever way it is. At the same time, cricket is something which has always given me happiness, and batting is something which I've been enjoying throughout my career,” she said. “Today, and whenever I'm going to step in, I just want to enjoy my batting.” Harmanpreet, Pratika keep the approach simple India were in trouble at 19 for two after captain Smriti Mandhana fell for a duck, but Harmanpreet and Pratika Rawal steadied the innings with a crucial partnership. Rawal scored 61 off 67 deliveries, while the pair added 124 runs for the third wicket to put India back on track. Harmanpreet said the plan was to respect Zimbabwe's good deliveries while capitalising on anything loose, with both batters clear about their approach in the ODI format. “Well, today we were playing an ODI format, and in ODI format, you have to act differently. That's what Pratika and I both decided, that we have to respect if they're bowling in the right areas, and at the same time, if we're getting any loose ball, we have to punish that,” she said. “I think it was a very simple and clear message we gave each other, and then just reacting.” The India batter's innings laid the foundation for a record-breaking stand with Deepti, who accelerated through the middle and death overs to bring up her century off 83 balls. Their 153-run partnership was India's highest for the fifth wicket in women's ODIs. ‘You want to take responsibility for the team’ Harmanpreet also stressed that her focus while batting remained on the team's needs rather than on her own position or role. Asked whether her current form made her miss captaincy less, she said she approached every innings with the same sense of responsibility. “When you're batting, you don't think these kinds of things. When you're batting, you're batting as a batter, and you want to take responsibility for the team,” she said. “I'm somebody who likes to take responsibility and bat according to the situation, and no matter whatever the situation is, I just want to enjoy myself.” Harmanpreet reveals she battled fever Despite spending nearly 45 overs at the crease in the afternoon heat, Harmanpreet revealed that she had not been at her best physically. The India batter said she had a mild fever the previous night and was struggling after returning to the field. “Yeah, definitely. I actually had a mild fever last night. That's why I was struggling when we came back to the field, and I just wanted to, you know, take some rest,” she said. She added that medication was helping and expressed hope that she would recover soon. “I think the painkillers, everything, are helping me, and hopefully I'll come back stronger,'' she signed-off.

item.title: Why trade deadline should not have Eagles’ Howie Roseman fire selling for 2027 NFL Draft picks
item.description: Why trade deadline should not have Eagles’ Howie Roseman fire selling for 2027 NFL Draft picks appeared first on ClutchPoints . Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here . The Philadelphia Eagles are spiraling, and nobody sees any end in sight. Their franchise quarterback is facing a potentially season-ending medical absence. Philly’s offense has lost the identity that made it so dangerous. Naturally, the temptation to sell veterans for 2027 NFL Draft picks will grow as the trade deadline approaches . General manager Howie Roseman , though, must resist the urge to dismantle the roster. Philadelphia has too much invested in its current core to make a panic-driven decision. The Eagles, instead, need a measured retooling, not a scorched-earth rebuild. Season unraveled Edward Finan-Imagn Images Philadelphia opened the 2026 season with consecutive victories over Washington and Tennessee. That created hope that the team could quickly reestablish itself among the NFC’s top contenders. The momentum disappeared in a hurry. A 27-7 loss to Chicago exposed significant problems in the passing game. It was followed by a 24-20 defeat to the Los Angeles Rams. Philadelphia then fell 19-17 to Jacksonville in London before losing 25-14 at home to Carolina. The four-game skid dropped the Eagles to 2-4. Their offense struggling to sustain drives, and the ground game producing remarkably little . The situation became more serious when further medical testing revealed that Hurts had deep vein thrombosis and blood clots in both lungs. He is expected to miss the remainder of the season while undergoing treatment. Jalen Hurts ’ absence Hurts’ medical situation changes Philadelphia’s immediate outlook. That said, it does not automatically make the team’s veteran core expendable. The Eagles should prioritize his health and avoid making assumptions about his return timetable. His doctors expect a full recovery without long-term effects. Still, he cannot participate in football activities while taking blood thinners. Hurts will eventually need proven protection, dependable receiving options, and a strong supporting cast. Dallas Goedert remains a valuable receiving option at tight end, while the offensive line is central to the team’s ability to establish a consistent attack. Naturally, the temptation to sell veterans for 2027 NFL Draft picks will grow as the trade deadline approaches . General manager Howie Roseman , though, must resist the urge to dismantle the roster. Philadelphia has too much invested in its current core to make a panic-driven decision. The Eagles, instead, need a measured retooling, not a scorched-earth rebuild. Season unraveled Edward Finan-Imagn Images Philadelphia opened the 2026 season with consecutive victories over Washington and Tennessee. That created hope that the team could quickly reestablish itself among the NFC’s top contenders. The momentum disappeared in a hurry. A 27-7 loss to Chicago exposed significant problems in the passing game. It was followed by a 24-20 defeat to the Los Angeles Rams. Philadelphia then fell 19-17 to Jacksonville in London before losing 25-14 at home to Carolina. The four-game skid dropped the Eagles to 2-4. Their offense struggling to sustain drives, and the ground game producing remarkably little . The situation became more serious when further medical testing revealed that Hurts had deep vein thrombosis and blood clots in both lungs. He is expected to miss the remainder of the season while undergoing treatment. Jalen Hurts ’ absence Hurts’ medical situation changes Philadelphia’s immediate outlook. That said, it does not automatically make the team’s veteran core expendable. The Eagles should prioritize his health and avoid making assumptions about his return timetable. His doctors expect a full recovery without long-term effects. Still, he cannot participate in football activities while taking blood thinners. Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) That uncertainty makes it even more important for Roseman to preserve a functional roster. Hurts will eventually need proven protection, dependable receiving options, and a strong supporting cast. Trading away established contributors for mid-round picks could leave Philadelphia with even fewer answers. Dallas Goedert remains a valuable receiving option at tight end, while the offensive line is central to the team’s ability to establish a consistent attack. Roseman should not entertain offers for core starters simply because the season has veered off course. A first-round pick or an exceptional offer might change the conversation. The default, though, should be to protect the foundation around Hurts. Don’t sell the foundation The Eagles also have a responsibility to the players still competing every week. Nick Sirianni and defensive coordinator Vic Fangio must continue developing the roster and evaluating which pieces can help the team recover in 2027. Stripping away productive veterans would undermine those efforts. Young defensive cornerstones such as Jalen Carter , Quinyon Mitchell, and Cooper DeJean need a competitive environment. They also need experienced teammates who understand how to prepare for high-pressure games. Removing too many veterans would leave Philadelphia asking its younger players to carry responsibilities they may not yet be ready to shoulder. Also, the remaining games still offer useful information. Tanner McKee’s performances can help the organization evaluate its quarterback depth . The coaching staff can assess whether the offense needs personnel changes, schematic adjustments or both. Those evaluations require a functioning team, not a roster reduced to replacement-level talent. Targeted retooling Rejecting a complete teardown does not mean Roseman should sit idle. Philadelphia can listen to offers for veterans nearing the end of their contracts or surplus depth pieces. If another team presents an attractive package for a nonessential player, the Eagles should consider it. The key is setting a clear threshold. Roseman should demand meaningful value and avoid creating new holes simply to accumulate future picks. Day-two and day-three selections can become important contributors, but they are not guaranteed replacements for proven NFL starters. Philadelphia also needs to assess its offensive structure. The team’s recent struggles demand honest questions about play-calling, protection, and the ability to sustain drives. Draft capital can help address those issues, but so can strategic free-agent additions and a more consistent offensive plan. Roseman has built his reputation on aggressive roster management. His next move should be to identify the right changes without sacrificing their core. Focus on the long game Bill Streicher-Imagn Images Nobody can deny that the Eagles have a number of serious problems. Hurts’ absence makes the road ahead considerably more difficult. Their 2-4 record is a legitimate warning sign. With that, Roseman should remain open to smart trades while protecting the team’s foundational talent. Philadelphia needs to evaluate its coaching and prepare for Hurts’ eventual return without making reckless decisions in the meantime. That said, selling veterans for a handful of future picks will provide only a temporary sense of direction. The Eagles need a disciplined retooling that preserves their competitive identity. Roseman must resist the panic and give this roster a chance to contend again when its franchise quarterback is ready. item.title: Luka Doncic reveals why he let Austin Reaves take the biggest shot despite scoring 52 points
item.description: Photo by Luke Hales/Getty Images Luka Doncic explained why he passed to Austin Reaves for a crucial late three-pointer despite scoring 52 points in the Los Angeles Lakers’ 132-123 victory over the Utah Jazz. The Slovenian superstar helped the Lakers recover from an 18-point deficit, delivering a historic performance as Los Angeles improved to 3-0 this season. However, when the game was on the line, Doncic trusted his teammate to deliver rather than chase another basket himself. Luka Doncic explains why he trusted Austin Reaves in crunch time Speaking to Lakers reporter Mike Trudell after the game, Doncic offered a straightforward explanation for his decision to pass. “Yeah, of course. I mean, he was wide open, and I missed the previous three,” Doncic said. Reaves made the most of the opportunity, knocking down a 25-foot three-pointer with 34 seconds remaining to extend the Lakers’ lead to seven points. The guard finished with 29 points and 11 rebounds, shooting four-for-five from beyond the arc. His contribution proved crucial alongside Doncic’s remarkable scoring display. Doncic had already reached 50 points with a three-pointer late in the fourth quarter before setting up Reaves on the decisive possession. He then added two free throws to finish with 52 points, eight rebounds and 10 assists. The performance also made NBA history. According to The Athletic’s Law Murray, Doncic became the first Lakers player since Elgin Baylor in 1963 to record at least 50 points and 10 assists in the same game. Despite the individual numbers, Doncic was more concerned about how his team started. “We had a terrible first quarter,” he told Trudell, after Los Angeles conceded 47 points in the opening period. “We learned our lesson, so we cannot start games like this anymore,” he added, highlighting the need for better defensive intensity. Doncic also praised the group developing around him, saying: “I think we have a great group, and you know, I love playing with these guys.” The Lakers have started the season unbeaten, and Doncic’s decision to trust Reaves offered another sign of their growing chemistry. Maintaining that connection will be important as Los Angeles looks to build on its promising opening run. item.content:encoded: Photo by Luke Hales/Getty Images Luka Doncic explained why he passed to Austin Reaves for a crucial late three-pointer despite scoring 52 points in the Los Angeles Lakers’ 132-123 victory over the Utah Jazz. The Slovenian superstar helped the Lakers recover from an 18-point deficit, delivering a historic performance as Los Angeles improved to 3-0 this season. However, when the game was on the line, Doncic trusted his teammate to deliver rather than chase another basket himself. Luka Doncic explains why he trusted Austin Reaves in crunch time Speaking to Lakers reporter Mike Trudell after the game, Doncic offered a straightforward explanation for his decision to pass. “Yeah, of course. I mean, he was wide open, and I missed the previous three,” Doncic said. Reaves made the most of the opportunity, knocking down a 25-foot three-pointer with 34 seconds remaining to extend the Lakers’ lead to seven points. The guard finished with 29 points and 11 rebounds, shooting four-for-five from beyond the arc. His contribution proved crucial alongside Doncic’s remarkable scoring display. Doncic had already reached 50 points with a three-pointer late in the fourth quarter before setting up Reaves on the decisive possession. He then added two free throws to finish with 52 points, eight rebounds and 10 assists. The performance also made NBA history. According to The Athletic’s Law Murray, Doncic became the first Lakers player since Elgin Baylor in 1963 to record at least 50 points and 10 assists in the same game. Despite the individual numbers, Doncic was more concerned about how his team started. “We had a terrible first quarter,” he told Trudell, after Los Angeles conceded 47 points in the opening period. “We learned our lesson, so we cannot start games like this anymore,” he added, highlighting the need for better defensive intensity. Doncic also praised the group developing around him, saying: “I think we have a great group, and you know, I love playing with these guys.” The Lakers have started the season unbeaten, and Doncic’s decision to trust Reaves offered another sign of their growing chemistry. Maintaining that connection will be important as Los Angeles looks to build on its promising opening run. item.title: African players in Europe: Jackson brace ends City's perfect record
item.description: Nicolas Jackson (L) scores his second goal for Aston Villa against Manchester City at Villa Park (Darren Staples) Senegal star Nicolas Jackson took his goal tally since joining Aston Villa from Chelsea to seven in 11 matches by bagging a brace in a 2-1 Premier League win over Manchester City at the weekend. Victory for Villa ended a seven-match winning streak by City since the league season began. City still top the table, but only on goal difference from defending champions Arsenal. AFP Sport highlights African headline-makers in the major European leagues: ENGLAND NICOLAS JACKSON (Aston Villa) Jackson put Villa ahead in the sixth minute with a fine finish into the roof of the net from John McGinn's pass. After Erling Haaland equalised for the leaders in the 52nd minute, Jackson clinched a memorable win for Villa eight minutes later. Teenage Senegal international Ibrahim Mbaye teed up Jackson to squeeze his shot past City goalkeeper Gianluigi Donnarumma. DANGO OUATTARA (Brentford) The Burkina Faso winger scored for the first time this season to rescue a 1-1 draw at Hull City. Ouattara slotted home in the 63rd minute from Igor Thiago's pass. The 24-year-old cancelled out Oli McBurnie’s first half penalty, but Brentford were left without a win in their last three games. SPAIN INAKI WILLIAMS (Athletic Bilbao) After Spain 2026 World Cup winner Nico Williams came close to scoring, older brother and Ghana international Inaki struck the second goal in a 4-0 La Liga romp against Getafe. A counterattack ended with Inaki Williams one-on-one against the Getafe goalkeeper and he netted with a low shot. ITALY ANDRE-FRANK ANGUISSA (Napoli) Cameroon midfielder Anguissa sent a brilliant bicycle kick into the corner of the net on 28 minutes after Roma failed to clear a free-kick. It was the opening goal of a 3-3 Serie A thriller. GERMANY SERHOU GUIRASSY (Borussia Dortmund) Guirassy was kept off the scoresheet, but posed a constant threat as Borussia beat Eintracht Frankfurt 1-0 at home. Early in the opening half, the Guinea international was through on goal, but had his chip saved by goalkeeper Noah Atubolu. Just after the break, Guirassy headed a corner against the bar and went close again when he hit a cross inches wide of the left post. FRANCE ELYE WAHI, SOFIANE DIOP (Nice) Internationals Wahi of the Ivory Coast and Diop of Morocco scored as mid-table Nice came from behind to win 2-1 at Brest in Ligue 1. Wahi equalised just past the hour mark after a corner and Diop punished a defensive blunder to grab the 83rd-minute winner. bur-dl/ea

item.title: Bryce Young, Dave Canales left shell-shocked by Panthers’ disgusting loss to Buccaneers
item.description: Jim Dedmon-Imagn Images Bryce Young, Dave Canales left shell-shocked by Panthers’ disgusting loss to Buccaneers appeared first on ClutchPoints . Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here . It looked like Bryce Young and Dave Canales were disconnected in the Carolina Panthers ’ blowout loss to the Tampa Bay Buccaneers, 43-13, at Bank of America Stadium on Sunday. Well, they were on the same page after it, at least. Young and Canales were disgusted with their anemic performance. They suffered from a terrible start, scoring only six points in the first half and giving up 33 points to the Buccaneers. Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) “Obviously, (it was) not Panthers football. Not something we want to do,” said Young, as quoted by FOX Sports Radio1340’s Sheena Quick. Canales said the loss “was a shock” to the system, acknowledging that they have to play “better football.” “Literally, I’ve never been part of a half of football like that. To experience it in all phases: Block-kick, sack-fumble, interception, a drop punt. Then the defensive side really just not getting off the field in different ways,” said Canales. “Shoot, it was just like, I don’t know. It just felt so crazy and so egregiously different to the ball we’re used to playing. I’m gonna look at the things and see what was technical about it, what the execution was, and look at all those things.” Dave Canales says today’s performance was “a shock”. “Literally, I’ve never been part of a half of football like that.” #Panthers pic.twitter.com/Haq7PLjBcT — Sheena Quick (@Sheena_Marie3) October 25, 2026 Young went 14-of-27 for 163 yards, one touchdown, and two interceptions. He was sacked five times. He was replaced by Kenny Pickett in the closing minutes. The Panthers scored their lowest output of the season and had four turnovers. Carolina fell to 3-3, while Tampa Bay improved to 2-5. The loss was extra costly for Carolina, as Taylor Moton suffered an ankle injury in the third quarter and did not return. He missed the first four weeks due to blood clots in his lungs. Related: Panthers’ Bryce Young benched for Kenny Pickett late in total no-show vs. Buccaneers Related: Panthers on major fraud watch in Baker Mayfield’s return, and now there’s a bad injury on top of it

item.title: Jalen Brunson sends key message to Knicks after ugly 0-3 start to title defense
item.description: Wendell Cruz-Imagn Images Jalen Brunson sends key message to Knicks after ugly 0-3 start to title defense appeared first on ClutchPoints . Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here . Jalen Brunson took responsibility for the New York Knicks ’ struggles after they fell to 0-3 this season following their 111-102 loss to the Orlando Magic on Sunday night. Brunson and New York started their title defense this season. He led the franchise to their first championship since 1973 after beating the San Antonio Spurs in the 2026 NBA Finals. However, the start to the campaign has been rough. They lost their first three contests to the Philadelphia 76ers, the Boston Celtics and the Magic. Brunson reflected on these struggles after the game, per ESPN. Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) “Everything falls on my shoulders,” Brunson said, in reference to the Knicks’ potent offense sputtering in the opening days of the season. “I just gotta be a better leader when it comes to that, when it comes to our guys are ready to go in the right spots. There’s a lot of other little things, but it’s organization on my part.” Brunson also revealed to reporters about the message he had shared with teammates in the locker room following the loss. “Control what you can control… most importantly stick together,” Brunson said. “One thing I said throughout the entire training camp, and honestly to this day, is we’re going to see who we are within the first couple weeks of the season. So we’re hitting adversity now, how are we going to respond?” Jalen Brunson talks about the message in the locker room after starting the season 0-3: "Control what you can control… most importantly stick together." pic.twitter.com/PuHRv0pXTF — SNY Knicks (@sny_knicks) October 26, 2026 How Jalen Brunson, Knicks played against Magic Jalen Brunson and the Knicks have the talent to bounce back from their slow start to the season. However, as the reigning champions, opponents will have motivation to pull off upsets against them. Four players scored in double-digits for New York in the loss, including Brunson. He led the squad with a stat line of 28 points, four assists, three rebounds, two steals, and one block. Karl-Anthony Towns came next with 22 points and 14 rebounds, OG Anunoby had 22 points and three rebounds, while Josh Hart provided 13 points and eight rebounds. The Knicks will continue the search for their first win. They remain at home when they host the Detroit Pistons as tip-off starts on Oct. 27 at 8 p.m. ET. Related: Mike Brown gets brutally honest as Knicks’ winless streak continues after loss to Magic Related: Knicks HC Mike Brown gets 100% real about decision to cut player for Dalton Knecht

item.title: Mourinho keeps Clasico midas touch 13 years on as La Liga heats up
item.description: Real Madrid have now won five consecutive games in all competitions [Getty Images] Jose Mourinho has done it again. The Real Madrid manager celebrated Kylian Mbappe's late winner at Barcelona on Sunday with a trademark knee slide, as he maintained his midas touch over their bitter rivals. Mourinho has become just the third Real boss to go six El Clasicos in a row without defeat - 13 years after he last led Los Blancos in this fixture. Four wins and two draws in his past six matches in charge of Real Madrid against Barcelona puts him up there with Miguel Munoz (1962 to 1965) and Vicente del Bosque (2001 to 2003). It was also just a second victory in eight games against Barcelona for Real, with the return of Mourinho to the fixture haunting the reigning champions And more importantly for Mourinho, Mbappe's double in Real's 2-1 win ended Barcelona's nine-game unbeaten domestic run with a crucial Clasico victory at the Camp Nou. A Real defeat would have allowed Barcelona to establish a commanding nine-point advantage but the result has transformed the top of La Liga, bringing Mourinho's side to within three points of their rivals. "In my view, Real Madrid do not play to win at the Camp Nou, Real Madrid play to win La Liga," Mourinho said. "We could win with luck, but we won with calmness and with all merit," he said. "It's a very strong group. Everyone works very hard. Everyone was ready to win. "The credit goes to the players. When you win, the credit goes to the players. But when you lose, the blame falls on you. And that's why we see coaches being sacked from their positions every week." The Portuguese has now won six and lost six El Clasicos across his two stints as manager. He said: "I've learned that I have an extraordinary group, with the quality and mindset to play. "In midfield, having a mix of talents gives us more than just having two players with similar characteristics. This mix of talents gives us balance when defending and quality when we go on the attack. "We've beaten several teams by four or more goals, but this is Barca, and the players put on a great performance. We need to continue like this and don't go over the moon after this win." Barcelona boss Hansi Flick said he did not want to give excuses for the defeat but admitted his team lacked fresh legs after a demanding few weeks. "We missed the freshness," he said. "It's not easy for our players. We have to recover well, train well and we have to respond from this defeat. "In big games, small things are important and they decide the games and today, it wasn't on our side. "I can see that today we were not fresh and this is what we have to change." Mbappe double fires Real Madrid to win at leaders Barcelona Listen to the latest Football Daily podcast Get football news sent straight to your phone

item.title: It’s time for Raiders to give Fernando Mendoza the keys after 4 straight losses with Kirk Cousins
item.description: Kirk Cousins and Fernando Mendoza . It’s time for Raiders to give Fernando Mendoza the keys after 4 straight losses with Kirk Cousins appeared first on ClutchPoints . Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here . Coach Klint Kubiak’s struggling Las Vegas Raiders have lost four straight games following their 14-point home loss to the Los Angeles Rams at Allegiant Stadium in Las Vegas, giving fans, and the head coach, a lot to think about. The Raiders got injury news on running back Mike Washington Jr. heading into Week 7’s game against the Rams and watched as he played, recording 27 yards on a mostly drab day. Quarterback Kirk Cousins was a bright spot with 295 yards and two touchdowns on the day, but fans wondered aloud if it may be time to move on to number one overall draft pick Fernando Mendoza after another Raiders game turned into a loss with time running out to salvage the season. Cousins has now completed less than 60 percent of his passes in three of the last four games, another strike against him as Kubiak decides whether or not to give the rookie a chance to lead soon. Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) With the New York Jets on deck for Week 8, now is the perfect time for Kubiak to give the keys to the car to Mendoza, who can help restore and revitalize a fanbase that is looking for something, anything to get excited about during what has felt like another wasted season lately. Kirk Cousins’ accuracy is waning David Brytus-Imagn Images Cousins completed 26-of-44 passes against the Rams, and that won’t get it done in the bigger games of the season. Cousins is known for his accuracy and command of whatever offense he plays for, but one of his best traits appears to be leaving him at this crucial juncture of his career with Las Vegas. Cousins has done his best to rally the troops and fire them up with pregame speeches, but it hasn’t helped a whole lot as the Raiders still appear overmatched, listless, and ready to check out most of the time. The Raiders have given Cousins plenty of opportunities to show he can still lead a team deep into the playoffs, but he simply isn’t getting the job done. His 295-yard, two touchdown stat line shows he can still be an effective NFL quarterback, but the mood around the Raiders is starting to go south as fans, players and coaches all appear to be waiting around for the inevitable to happen; namely, for Mendoza to finally show what he can do on the football field for the first time in extended regular season action this year. Delaying the inevitable isn’t fair to Cousins, the Raiders’ fans, or anyone else. Mendoza should get his chance against coach Aaron Glenn’s Jets in Week 8. item.content:encoded: Kirk Cousins and Fernando Mendoza . It’s time for Raiders to give Fernando Mendoza the keys after 4 straight losses with Kirk Cousins appeared first on ClutchPoints . Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here . Coach Klint Kubiak’s struggling Las Vegas Raiders have lost four straight games following their 14-point home loss to the Los Angeles Rams at Allegiant Stadium in Las Vegas, giving fans, and the head coach, a lot to think about. The Raiders got injury news on running back Mike Washington Jr. heading into Week 7’s game against the Rams and watched as he played, recording 27 yards on a mostly drab day. Quarterback Kirk Cousins was a bright spot with 295 yards and two touchdowns on the day, but fans wondered aloud if it may be time to move on to number one overall draft pick Fernando Mendoza after another Raiders game turned into a loss with time running out to salvage the season. Cousins has now completed less than 60 percent of his passes in three of the last four games, another strike against him as Kubiak decides whether or not to give the rookie a chance to lead soon. Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) With the New York Jets on deck for Week 8, now is the perfect time for Kubiak to give the keys to the car to Mendoza, who can help restore and revitalize a fanbase that is looking for something, anything to get excited about during what has felt like another wasted season lately. Kirk Cousins’ accuracy is waning David Brytus-Imagn Images Cousins completed 26-of-44 passes against the Rams, and that won’t get it done in the bigger games of the season. Cousins is known for his accuracy and command of whatever offense he plays for, but one of his best traits appears to be leaving him at this crucial juncture of his career with Las Vegas. Cousins has done his best to rally the troops and fire them up with pregame speeches, but it hasn’t helped a whole lot as the Raiders still appear overmatched, listless, and ready to check out most of the time. The Raiders have given Cousins plenty of opportunities to show he can still lead a team deep into the playoffs, but he simply isn’t getting the job done. His 295-yard, two touchdown stat line shows he can still be an effective NFL quarterback, but the mood around the Raiders is starting to go south as fans, players and coaches all appear to be waiting around for the inevitable to happen; namely, for Mendoza to finally show what he can do on the football field for the first time in extended regular season action this year. Delaying the inevitable isn’t fair to Cousins, the Raiders’ fans, or anyone else. Mendoza should get his chance against coach Aaron Glenn’s Jets in Week 8. Mendoza needs time to put his stamp on the team Mendoza has an infectious personality and great leadership skills, similar to Cousins, but it’s going to take time for him to implement them on a Raiders team in desperate need of hope, and a new direction. Kubiak talked about what the Raiders need to do after the game, but his words fell on deaf ears as fans once again began to question his decision-making. Mendoza is not any old rookie quarterback; he carries the clout and presence of a national championship winning player who lifted one of college football’s worst programs, the Indiana Hoosiers, to national championship status during his time with Curt Cignetti in Bloomington, Indiana. Mendoza is deadly accurate, athletic, a plus runner, and a caretaker of the football who will likely be just as accurate, or perhaps even more accurate than Cousins by the time he settles in with offensive coordinator Andrew Janocko’s unit. His ability to run when a play breaks down will add a whole new dimension to Janocko’s offense, giving fans something new to cheer about as the Raiders prepare to face the Jets in Week 8. Raiders’ supporting cast can ease the transition The Raiders’ supporting cast is better than it’s shown this season and Cousins is holding them back. If he can’t complete more than 60 percent of his passes with guys like Ashton Jeanty, Michael Mayer, recent injury returnee Brock Bowers , Jalen Nailor and Tre Tucker at his side, it’s a sign that he is starting to lose some of the talents that have made him one of the NFL’s best QBs for years now. The Raiders need more efficiency and more big-play potential from their offense, something that Mendoza can bring within the first few weeks as their new starting quarterback. Cousins still has the quarterbacking chops to stay in the league as a backup, but he needs to start leading the Raiders to wins or he will be replaced. Mendoza can perform just as well as Cousins while bringing hope and joy to a franchise in dire need of both. It’s time for Kubiak to hand the keys to his vehicle to Mendoza, or else risk losing the Raiders’ fanbase, and the season, while waiting around for something to change. item.title: ‘Lost his accuracy and nerve’ – Skip Bayless’ cold assessment of Patrick Mahomes in Chiefs loss
item.description: Photo by Steph Chambers/Getty Images The Kansas City Chiefs fell to their first loss of the 2026 NFL season with a 20-3 performance against the Seattle Seahawks. Chiefs QB Patrick Mahomes struggled to come up with answers for the Seahawks’ defence, going 19/33 on pass attempts for 165 yards, 0 touchdowns, and one interception for a 58.3 passer rating. This was the first game in Mahomes’ career where he did not have a red zone drive, and it led to the Chiefs losing their first game of the season. Skip Bayless’ blunt take on Patrick Mahomes Bayless shared his thoughts on X in the second quarter about the Mahomes’ performance he was witnessing, thoroughly unimpressed by the two-time regular-season MVP. “Mahomes has lost his accuracy and nerve. This is a mismatch. Seattle 35-7.” Bayless would add to his thoughts in a later post, referring to Mahomes as a ‘Sunday Nightmare’ after a Harrison Butker missed field goal. “Mahomes is a Sunday Nightmare. So is Butker.” Mahomes looked out of sorts in the first game of the season where the Chiefs were comfortably outplayed. The Seahawks used a very aggressive, high-pressure defensive line to not only force Mahomes into bad decisions but also completely neutralise the rush threat of Kenneth Walker III. While Bayless’ score prediction did not end up coming true, he correctly highlighted that this game was a mismatch before the first half had even ended. The Seahawks won a Super Bowl on the back of this defence 10 months ago, and they showed up to hand the Chiefs their first loss of the season in emphatic fashion. Mahomes has had a strong season overall with 124/191 on pass attempts for 1,474 total yards, nine touchdowns, four interceptions and a passer rating of 95.3. item.content:encoded: Minnesota are the NFL's last remaining undefeated team after Travis Kelce's Kansas City lost at Seattle [Getty Images] Week seven of the NFL left one unbeaten team standing and few - if any - would have picked them out at the start of the season. The Kansas City Chiefs were beaten at defending champions the Seattle Seahawks while the San Francisco 49ers also suffered their first loss. But the Minnesota Vikings marched on to maintain their 100% record, and there were also big wins for the Cleveland Browns and Denver Broncos. Here are the biggest stories from Sunday's games in the NFL. Seahawks show championship pedigree Kansas City and Seattle have not only won three of the past four Super Bowls, they came into week seven with this season's best offence and best defence respectively, in terms of total yards. Sunday's primetime match also marked the return of Kenneth Walker, the Most Valuable Player in last season's Super Bowl, to former team Seattle after joining the Chiefs in the off-season. The running back has made a stunning start with Kansas City, leading the NFL in rushing yards per game (133) after six weeks, but Seattle's defence was determined to show why they became known as 'the Dark Side' during last season's championship run. They stifled Patrick Mahomes and the Chiefs, restricting Walker to 36 yards from 14 carries as KC tied for their fewest points in a game with Mahomes as their starting quarterback. Seattle quarterback Sam Darnold also continued to lean on Jaxon Smith-Njigba, with last season's offensive player of the year claiming 150 receiving yards and a touchdown, while new running back Emanuel Wilson finished with 100 rushing yards and a score. The Seahawks ran out 20-3 winners to improve their record to 4-3, while the Chiefs are now 5-1. Purdy blots copybook Brock Purdy went to the top of the all-time list for career passer rating last week but did not hit his normal high standards as the San Francisco quarterback was frustrated by the Atlanta Falcons. The hosts forced four turnovers, including two Purdy interceptions, as they won 29-20 to inflict a first loss on the new Super Bowl favourites. The 49ers are 6-1 while NFC West rivals the Los Angeles Rams - the pre-season favourites - got back to winning ways. The Rams are 3-4 after winning 35-21 at the Las Vegas Raiders, where Matt Stafford became the first player to lead two teams for touchdown passes. Last season's MVP previously set the franchise record for the Detroit Lions before joining the Rams in 2021. They next face the Los Angeles Chargers, who are the last remaining winless team after the Miami Dolphins won 28-25 at the New York Jets. Vikings stretch surprise run For the first time in the NFL, two divisions will go into week eight with all four teams having a record better than 50%. One of those is the NFC North, topped by the Minnesota Vikings. Before the season, half the NFL was considered to have a better chance of winning the Super Bowl. But they are the last undefeated team at 6-0 after coming from behind to win 16-10 at home to the Indianapolis Colts. Their defence has been one of the league's best, Will Reichard is yet to miss a kick and - although their offence is yet to catch fire - the Vikings keep grinding out victories. Including the end of last season, Kevin O'Connell's team are on an 11-game win streak, but they face a test at divisional rivals Detroit next week. After naming new signing Kyler Murray as their starting quarterback, the Vikings traded JJ McCarthy four weeks ago and he impressed on his first start for the New York Giants on Sunday, leading them to a 27-21 win in overtime at the Houston Texans. Elsewhere in the NFC North, Jessie Bates kicked a field goal as time expired to hand the Detroit Lions a 20-17 win over the Green Bay Packers. Only three field-goal attempts have been missed from inside 35 yards all season and Green Bay rookie Trey Smack missed two of them on Sunday. Watson keeps Browns on top Deshaun Watson came into this season with a 9-10 record in four years with Cleveland [Getty Images] All AFC North teams also have at least four wins, with the Pittsburgh Steelers kicking off Sunday's action by beating the New Orleans Saints 16-10 in the NFL's first game in France. The Cleveland Browns (5-2) then regained top spot after Andre Szmyt made his third game-winning kick in four weeks to claim a 27-24 win at the Tennessee Titans. Deshaun Watson was booed by Cleveland fans in pre-season but has now led five game-winning drives this season and is beginning to look like the player he was at Houston, which convinced the Browns to sign him on a fully-guaranteed deal in 2022 worth $230m (£172m). Their other divisional rivals went head-to-head. The Baltimore Ravens had to manage without quarterback Lamar Jackson for a third straight game and led the Cincinnati Bengals 13-0 at half-time. But the Bengals stormed back to win 35-13, with Joe Burrow throwing for four touchdowns and 292 yards as the Ravens suffered a second straight loss. Baltimore have not set a return date for two-time MVP Jackson (ankle) and have a tough trip to the Buffalo Bills next week. Titans release Elliott for pulling gun in car park Broncos back near their best Bo Nix's leap into the endzone capped the longest run of his career, which nearly trebled his rushing yards for the season [Getty Images] The Denver Broncos earned the top seed in the AFC Conference last season but, although they beat Buffalo in the divisional round, the win was overshadowed by a late injury to Bo Nix. A broken ankle meant the Broncos had to do without their starting quarterback the following week as the New England Patriots denied them a spot in the Super Bowl. Over their first six games of the season, some questioned whether two off-season surgeries had impacted on his ability to run the ball, which had been a valuable weapon for Denver. Nix had also struggled with his arm. But the third-year quarterback responded in style, rushing for a 62-yard touchdown against the Arizona Cardinals - the longest QB run since 2022. Nix finished with 222 passing yards and a touchdown pass as the Broncos won 30-16 to go 5-2 in the AFC West behind Kansas City, who they host next week. item.title: Nikola Jokic has stern words for fans who booed Nuggets before comeback win
item.description: Mandatory Credit: Christopher Hanewinckel-Imagn Images Nikola Jokic has stern words for fans who booed Nuggets before comeback win appeared first on ClutchPoints . Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here . Nikola Jokic had a message for the fans who booed the Denver Nuggets , and he delivered it rather bluntly after Saturday’s home opener . “We got booed at our first home game, and I think those fans who booed us, they don’t need to come anymore,” said Jokic after the 141-135 overtime win over the New Orleans Pelicans. “If you guys follow us, you know that we never quit and we’ve come back from much worse situations.” Nikola Jokic has a message for the fans that were booing the Nuggets in the first half: Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) "They are not welcome anymore." pic.twitter.com/cZR2cr5ku7 — Rachel Strand (@MileHighRachel) October 25, 2026 The Nuggets got off to an unusually slow start in which they fell behind by 23 points. The Pelicans were shooting nearly lights out at 65.9% in the first half, which the Nuggets couldn’t keep up with. Denver fans would shower the team with boos as they headed to the locker room at the half down 73-57. Nuggets get booed and heckled as they head to the locker room at the half They're down 57-73 to the Pelicans. pic.twitter.com/kmlg0CecGl — Rachel Strand (@MileHighRachel) October 25, 2026 Regarding the sluggish start, Jokic was matter-of-fact with the reason why. The Nuggets weren’t hitting their shots, and the Pelicans were. He said they also needed a bit to work through some “bad energy.” After the half, the Nuggets finally managed to shake off that bad energy. Jokic would finish with 35 points, 15 rebounds, and 10 assists. This would be Jokic’s 199th regular-season triple-double, just narrowly trailing Russell Westbrook’s 209. Jamal Murray would also be a key part of the Nuggets’ comeback. He would record 42 points, as well as hitting a staggering eight three-pointers. Rookie Trevon Brazile also put on a show with 17 points, as well as some key blocks and defensive rebounds in crunch time. The Nuggets were playing shorthanded as they were without Cam Johnson (ankle sprain), Alpha Diallo (wrist sprain), and Julian Strawther (knee sprain). The Nuggets will look to start much faster against the Golden State Warriors when they come to town Monday night . Related: NBA rumors: Bucks walked away from Nuggets trade talks, but rival execs would’ve pulled trigger Related: Nuggets’ Nikola Jokic gets 1 step closer to NBA history with triple-double vs. Pelicans

item.title: Kenneth Walker Under Fire for Taking Surprising Action After 36-Yard Game vs. Seahawks
item.description: SEATTLE, WASHINGTON - OCTOBER 25: Kenneth Walker III #9 of the Kansas City Chiefs heads to the locker room before a game against the Seattle Seahawks at Lumen Field on October 25, 2026 in Seattle, Washington. (Photo by Steph Chambers/Getty Images) Getty Much has been made about Kenneth Walker joining the Kansas City Chiefs, but the Seattle Seahawks held the team’s former running back in check. Walker posted 14 carries for 36 rushing yards while averaging 2.6 yards per carry as Chiefs sustained their first loss of the NFL season. It was by far Walker’s worst outing since joining the Chiefs. Yet, it was Walker’s actions after the game that has fans’ attention. Walker appeared to run off the field without shaking any of his former Seahawks teammates hands. The Chiefs star’s actions drew attention on social media. “Kenneth Walker runs off the field without shaking hands with any of his former teammates or Mike MacDonald,” KREM2’s Andrew Quinn noted in an October 25, 2026, message on X. How are you feeling about Walker’s decision to bolt for the locker room immediately after the Chiefs’ loss to the Seahawks? Let us know in the comments below. Ex-Seahawks RB Kenneth Walker Appeared to Skip Postgame Handshake With Former Team After Chiefs’ Loss Players typically greet each other and shake hands after the game, especially when there are previous ties between the athlete and the team’s opponent. During the television broadcast, Walker appeared to head straight for the locker room instead of going on the field to greet his former teammates. “After being held to just 36 yards on 14 carries, Kenneth Walker III did not got to midfield to shake hands with Mike Macdonald or any of his former Seahawks teammates,” Football Forever noted while posting a video of Walker running off the field. “Walker III walked immediately to the locker room after the Chiefs’ 20-3 loss.” “Kenneth Walker got the HECK OUT OF THERE as soon as the game ended lol,” Xpand Sports’ Tanner Phifer remarked on X. This article was originally published on HEAVY The post Kenneth Walker Under Fire for Taking Surprising Action After 36-Yard Game vs. Seahawks appeared first on HEAVY .

item.title: Cole Caufield’s Canadiens claim will surely divide fans across Canada
item.description: Mandatory Credit: David Kirouac-Imagn Images Cole Caufield’s Canadiens claim will surely divide fans across Canada appeared first on ClutchPoints . Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here . The Montreal Canadiens are having a fine start to the 2026-27 NHL season. Cole Caufield and his teammates are looking to return to the Stanley Cup Playoffs. In outdoor conditions on Sunday, Caufield was a big star for the Habs against the Winnipeg Jets. The Canadiens defeated the Jets 2-1 in the Heritage Classic at Princess Auto Stadium in Winnipeg. Caufield provided an assist on both goals scored by the Habs. After the game, he made quite the claim about his team that could cause quite the divide across Canada. “Best fans in the league; they travel very well. We might be Canada’s favorite team. You can tell by tonight. Very lucky to play in these games, super fun,” he told TNT Sports on Sunday. Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) The Canadiens opened the scoring in the second period on Sunday night. Caufield delivered his first assist to defenseman Lane Hutson, who scored an incredible goal. Montreal then followed that up with a tally from defenseman Kaiden Guhle to make it 2-0. Winnipeg found a goal for itself in the third period. Unfortunately for them, it wasn’t enough. Habs netminder Jacob Fowler was a wall in the crease on Sunday night. And the Canadiens were able to clinch a big win outdoors. Montreal is 6-3-2 on the 2026-27 campaign, good for fifth in a loaded Atlantic Division. It’s still early, but the Canadiens have shown they can win some big games this year. They will need to continue stringing these wins together as the calendar flips to November. The Canadiens will look for their third win in a row against the St. Louis Blues on Tuesday night. item.title: Luka Doncic’s 52-point Eruption Moves Him Past Kevin Durant
item.description: Los Angeles Lakers v Houston Rockets Getty Luka Doncic gave the Los Angeles Lakers a 3-0 start Sunday while climbing past Kevin Durant in a different scoring race. His 52 points powered a 132-123 victory over the Utah Jazz, giving him 10 career games with at least 50 points. “Luka, he’s on the way,” Durant said in a March interview with Boardroom per Bleacher Report. “They’re hitting those marks that I hit at that time, that LeBron hit, Kobe hit at that age. … I just hope that moment is as special for them as it is for me passing the greats that I looked up to and watched when I was younger. I hope I left that impact on the game.” Doncic’s latest performance moved him ahead of Durant and Giannis Antetokounmpo in career 50-point outings. He also drew even with Kareem Abdul-Jabbar, sharing 11th place in NBA history. The milestone came during Los Angeles’ first road appearance this season. After opening with two home victories, the Lakers overcame an uneven beginning in Utah to keep their unbeaten record intact. Where does Luka Doncic stand among the NBA’s 50-point scorers? At 27, Doncic has reached double figures in career 50-point performances. His next such game would bring him level with Allen Iverson, who sits one ahead. Against Utah, Doncic converted 56.7% of his 30 field-goal attempts. He also connected at a 44.4% clip across 18 attempts from beyond the arc, combining volume with efficiency on his way to 52. He established his scoring rhythm immediately, accounting for Los Angeles’ opening six points. By the end of the first quarter, he had 17, even as the Lakers struggled to find their footing around him. Durant’s earlier comments concerned the broader pursuit of scoring milestones. Following Houston’s March 21 victory against Miami, his 32,294 career points placed him fifth on the league’s scoring leaderboard, ahead of Michael Jordan. That career-points ranking measures something different from the 50-point list Doncic climbed Sunday. Still, Durant had already identified Doncic as a player following the scoring benchmarks that he, LeBron James, and Kobe Bryant reached. Sunday supplied another milestone in that progression, with Doncic moving beyond Durant in the number of times each has reached 50. How does Doncic’s performance compare with Lakers scoring greats? Doncic also advanced within Lakers history, Yahoo reports. The Utah game marked his third 50-point performance for Los Angeles, matching James’ total during his Lakers tenure and putting Doncic fifth on the franchise list. According to StatMuse, that moved him beyond Shaquille O’Neal and Wilt Chamberlain. Bryant remains the franchise leader in 50-point games. The two lists give Doncic’s afternoon separate significance. His career total now matches Abdul-Jabbar’s, while his Lakers total matches James’. The comparisons reflect different stretches of his career, with only three of his 10 qualifying performances coming in a Los Angeles uniform. For the Lakers, the immediate result also

item.title: NFC Playoff Picture, Week 7: Seahawks climb back into NFC West race with win, 49ers loss
item.description: We’re not quite halfway through the 2026 NFL season, but the next time the Seattle Seahawks play a game will be November, so we might as well take a look at where they stand in the playoff hunt after their Week 7 win over the Kansas City Chiefs . What makes Seattle’s win over the Chiefs doubly important is the fact that the San Francisco 49ers lost 29-20 to the Atlanta Falcons, ending their undefeated run as they enter a bye week. While it would’ve been cool for the Los Angeles Rams to keep slumping and lose to the Las Vegas Raiders, that did not materialize, but they’re still behind the Seahawks in the NFC West battle. The Arizona Cardinals also lost. NFC West standings after Week 7 1. San Francisco 49ers (6-1, 3-0 NFCW) 2. Seattle Seahawks (4-3, 1-1 NFCW) 3. Los Angeles Rams (3-4, 1-2 NFCW) 4. Arizona Cardinals (2-5, 0-3 NFCW) In the bigger picture, the Seahawks are still out of a playoff spot due to the insane depth of the NFC North, in which every team is above .500. It’s not a thing to worry about right now, but it seems more likely than not that the NFC North will be the main competition for Seattle in terms of the Wild Card hunt. NFC playoff standings after Week 7 1. Minnesota Vikings (6-0) 2. San Francisco 49ers (6-1) 3. New York Giants (4-2-1) 4. Carolina Panthers (3-3) 5. Chicago Bears (5-2) 6. Detroit Lions (4-2) 7. Green Bay Packers (4-3) – Currently has tiebreaker on Seahawks due to better record vs. NFC (3-3 vs. 1-2) 8. Seattle Seahawks (4-3) 9. Atlanta Falcons (3-4, 3-2 NFC) 10. Los Angeles Rams (3-4, 2-2 NFC) 11. Philadelphia Eagles (2-4) – Monday Night Football 12. Dallas Cowboys (2-4) – Monday Night Football 13. Tampa Bay Buccaneers (2-5, 1-0 NFCS) 14. New Orleans Saints (2-5, 0-1 NFCS, 1-3 NFC) 15. Arizona Cardinals (2-5, 1-4 NFC) 16. Washington Commanders (1-4-1) Damn, that Commanders loss just really looks so annoying compared to Seattle’s other losses. But there’s still a lot of ball left, and the Seahawks still have reason to set their sights on the NFC West instead of effectively limiting their scope to the Wild Card chase.

item.title: ‘Real Madrid play to win the league!’ – Jose Mourinho fires warning to Barcelona despite dramatic Clasico victory
item.description: FC Barcelona v Real Madrid - LaLiga EA Sports 2026/27 - Getty Images Sport Jose Mourinho has warned his Real Madrid players to stay grounded following their dramatic 2-1 victory over Barcelona. The Portuguese coach insists the ultimate goal remains winning the Liga title, despite Kylian Mbappe's late heroics securing a massive win at Camp Nou. Mbappe shines in Clasico win Madrid secured a crucial 2-1 victory over Barca in Sunday's Clasico at Camp Nou. Mbappe proved to be the match-winner , scoring twice to close the gap at the top of the Liga table to just three points. The French forward opened the scoring in the 41st minute in fortunate fashion. Barcelona defender Gerard Martin attempted a clearance, but the ball rebounded directly off Mbappe and found the back of the net. Raphinha later levelled the scoreline for the hosts to set up a tense finish. However, Mbappe secured the victory in the 87th minute, finishing off a stunning counter-attack after receiving a precise pass from substitute Eduardo Camavinga. Mourinho demands league title focus Los Blancos have now secured five consecutive victories across all competitions. Despite this impressive run of form, Mourinho is determined to keep his squad entirely focused on the bigger picture. The Portuguese coach made it clear that a single victory over their fiercest rivals is not the ultimate prize. He wants his players to maintain their concentration for the remainder of the domestic campaign. "This is a great win, but when we get back to work, I'm not going to let anyone have their head in the clouds," Mourinho said, as quoted by ESPN . "If we win today and lose at El Sardinero [away at Racing Santander next weekend], Real Madrid don't play to win at Camp Nou, but rather to win the league. We have to keep going." A spectacle for the football world The latest edition of the famous fixture certainly delivered on its high pre-match expectations. Both sides attacked with obvious intent, creating a thrilling contest for supporters watching across the globe. Mourinho was quick to praise the overall quality of the match, as well as the application of his own players under intense pressure. "I think it was a great game," Mourinho noted. "A game at a high level, a game which the world that loves football stopped to see, and they weren't let down... In our case, the boys played an extraordinary game, well organised, focused, with a lot of courage. For me it's a great victory for the boys, against a great opponent. The boys deserve it." Attention turns to Racing Santander Madrid must now quickly shift their attention back to their regular domestic duties. They travel to El Sardinero this weekend to face Racing Santander. Los Blancos currently sit third in the La Liga standings with 24 points from ten matches - three points behind league leaders Barca and one point behind second-placed Atletico Madrid.

item.title: “Writing is on the wall”: Former Man United PL winner Ashley Young claims Michael Carrick’s future is inevitable
item.description: “Writing is on the wall”: Former Man United PL winner Ashley Young claims Michael Carrick’s future is inevitable Manchester United fell flat on their faces against AFC Bournemouth on Sunday afternoon. The match Three calamitous pieces of defending allowed the Cherries to score three goals at Old Trafford with ease. United now find themselves in 16th place, just one point above the relegation zone. They are also 14 points from the top of the table with just eight matches played, as the season has spiralled incredibly early on. As a result, Michael Carrick’s time as manager looks all but over, with Gary Neville claiming the club will probably sack him. Ashley Young comments Speaking to Sky Sports , Ashley Young claimed that it is inevitable that Carrick will now lose his job. Reviewing the performance of the players, Young stated, “players have got to stand up and be counted, but then of course you’re going to look at Ineos for what they did over the summer. They haven’t recruited the best and they haven’t got the players in.” Continuing to analyse the situation at the club, the former defender said, “as players, there’s no togetherness, there are individuals. They were all separated on the pitch and Bournemouth looked like the team that were on fire.” Defending his former teammate, he claimed, “it’s disappointing to see Michael Carrick like that. I wish there were players who knew and had the love for the club that he’s got. The players might look dejected, but I think Michael knows that the writing is on the wall.” Young refused to place too much blame on Carrick and asserted that the players are the constant theme. He explained, “there have been different managers [in recent seasons] but it’s the same players. There have been a few changes in players but they’re just not showing anything. You could tell today that it was like they’d given up – they’re not running for this manager and they’re not wanting to fight.” Finally, he sympathised with the supporters, stating that they “deserve so much more” and they have been constantly “let down” by the players over the years. Featured image by Dan Istitene via Getty Images online polls

item.title: Aaron Gordon Praises David Adelman's New System
item.description: The Denver Nuggets made a number of moves this offseason that while quiet, have contributed to a well-rounded bench that's given head coach David Adelman with a lot of pieces to work with when it comes to his rotations. Adelman himself even made the declaration that he'll be using as much of his bench as possible, even going so far as to possibly have an 11-man rotation to get as many of his players involved as possible. So far that's been the formula the Nuggets have employed and after the Nuggets' narrow victory over the New Orleans Pelicans, forward Aaron Gordon praised the new system and the role that he's had within it. Denver Nuggets forward Aaron Gordon (32) talks to his teammates during a time out against the Oklahoma City Thunder during the second half at Paycom Center. Alonzo Adams-Imagn Images Gordon Praises the System "I like the flow we have now, in and out, short stints on the bench opposed to long stints on the floor or long stints on the bench. The second unit is nice; it can be an extension of DA [head coach David Adelman] so I can be a floor general out there and a defensive general out there and kind of talk through what we are trying to get to," Gordon said (via Nuggets). Keeping everyone active is a system that works best for Gordon in particular after a 2025-26 season where Gordon was often held back by injuries. By not letting get too cold with a long stint on the bench while simultaneously keeping him from staying on his feet for too long, Gordon is in a much better position to stay heathy. Denver Nuggets forward Aaron Gordon (32) gestures after scoring a three point basket against the Oklahoma City Thunder during the second half at Paycom Center. Alonzo Adams-Imagn Images Gordon in particular also has a huge role in making Adelman's system effective. As he said, Gordon has the ability to be a floor general or a defensive anchor for the team depending on the rotation on the floor and that speaks to one of Gordon's greatest strengths: his versatility. Utilizing Versatility The Nuggets are able to play through Gordon in a variety of was because he can either be a principal playmaker or a pivot point on the floor, he can be a great defensive presence that makes things easier on the players around him or he can be a scoring leader in his own right. Denver Nuggets forward Aaron Gordon (32) fouls Oklahoma City Thunder guard Jalen Williams (8) as he shoots during the first half at Paycom Center. Alonzo Adams-Imagn Images His ability to matchup with anyone no matter who's on the court is one of the main reasons that Adelman's system will able to work moving forward and it will give the Nugget a whole host of options when it comes to game-planning for any opponents that come up. Gordon has always been one of the biggest hearts of the Nuggets as a whole and so long as he's able to stay healthy, Adelman may have found a way to utilize him to the best of his abilities in a completely new way and in the process, make the Nuggets a deep

item.title: Salech hails Moylan partnership for Cardiff
item.description: Cardiff City are six points of the Championship play-off spots and the relegation zone [Shutterstock] Yousef Salech believes he and Jack Moylan are proving mutually beneficial as Cardiff City improve their Championship fortunes. Salech scored the winner against Birmingham on Saturday after being included as a late starting change following a five-week injury absence. Cardiff planned to use him for a maximum 45 minutes, but he lasted the full 90 in atrocious conditions, while summer signing Moylan also played his part in the win. "I love playing with Jack. I hope he feels the same," said Salech. "He's more mobile than me, but probably I suck in more defenders closer to me and give him space so I hope and think we both benefit from playing with each other when we do." Salech ends Birmingham's unbeaten run on Cardiff return Cardiff's Aberfan inspiration after emotional tribute Salech's deft winner came in the 31st minute, making the most of Ollie Tanner's assist for the Dane's goal third in the league since the Bluebird's return to the second-tier for 2026-27. Ex-Birmingham player Krystian Bielik was stood down shortly before kick off after suffering a groin issue during the warm-up, prompting Salech's promotion to the starting line-up "two-and-half minutes" before kick off. Before grabbing the games only goal, last season's top scorer had earlier seen his penalty attempt saved by Blues keeper James Beadle. "I think the best thing as a player is to see it as any other chance in the game. I've missed a lot of chances in a lot of games. I've also missed penalties before," added Salech. "But that's not going to end the game. There's still 70 minutes left to play." Salech's Aberfan education The build-up to Saturday's encounter was filled with emotion, with boss Brian Barry-Murphy highlighting the importance of a fitting performance as they marked the Aberfan disaster of 1966. In the week before facing Birmingham, the Cardiff City squad and management visited Aberfan, taking in the graveyard where 116 children and 28 adults who died in the catastrophe are buried. Salech said: "First of all, I wasn't really educated or aware of this historic event before this week, but Brian and all of the staff of the club have informed us on Monday and we've seen almost a whole movie about it and also spoken between players." He added: "It was very emotional to get out there and see the memorial and speak to people who were involved and who were there that day that happened and speaking about their beloved ones and classmates and family members and everything. "And obviously I think it had a big impact on us on Tuesday and towards the build up towards the game... it seemed as though there was that little bit extra bite in every tackle, every chase for the ball. "That comes from a team doing well anyway, but I just thought if that had played a little bit into it, it could have." Latest Cardiff City news, analysis and fan views
