item.title: Marc Ter Stegen Reveals Ajax's 'Great Quality' After Win vs Sparta Rotterdam
item.description: Ajax vs Sparta Rotterdam Review! Ajax beat Sparta Rotterdam on Sunday, making it three wins in their last three games. Abdellah Ouazane put Ajax ahead with a brilliant finish. Jens Toornstra levelled the score with a header, but minutes later, Tolu Arokodare found the back of the net for the ninth time in an Ajax shirt to restore the lead for Michel Sanchez's side. In the first half, Ajax played quite well and had control of the game. In the second half, Sparta had several chances and put Ajax under serious pressure, but the Amsterdammers managed to hold onto their lead to secure the three points in Rotterdam. Ajax have now climbed above PSV Eindhoven in the Eredivisie title race and are only three points behind league leaders Feyenoord. There have been hiccups along the way, but Michel Sanchez has generally done a very good job so far. Ter Stegen opens up on Ajax's performance vs Sparta Marc ter Stegen had a very good game against Sparta. He made a couple of crucial saves in the second half to keep Ajax ahead. Speaking to ESPN after the game, Ter Stegen explained that he was pleased with Ajax's last three results. "My day was good. I am very happy with the past week," Ter Stegen said. "It was a big week with nine points from three matches. That is what we are looking for. Now we are putting other clubs under pressure." Ter Stegen also opened up on the performance against Sparta and admitted that the home side did not make it easy for them and that they had to suffer in the second half. "We didn't play very well," Ter Stegen said. "We scored twice, and sometimes that has to be enough. Later in the match, we had to suffer. If you know how to do that, it is a great quality to have." Ter Stegen went on to explain exactly what he meant by knowing how to 'suffer'. "Sometimes you also have to defend and accept that the other team is playing a good game. In the second half, they were better than us and put us under a lot of pressure. "Sometimes you have to accept that and make the best of it. You have to win your duels, and we did that. That is how I describe knowing how to suffer." item.title: The Hoddle of Coffee: Tottenham Hotspur News and Links for Monday, October 26
item.description: LONDON, ENGLAND - OCTOBER 18: Julie Blakstad of Tottenham Hotspur during the Barclays Women's Super League 2026/27 match between Chelsea FC and Tottenham Hotspur at Stamford Bridge on October 18, 2026 in London, England. (Photo by Catherine Ivill - AMA/Getty Images) | Getty Images Good morning everyone – I know the Chelsea result happened. But I’m travelling right now nad I’m writing this hoddle without knowing what the score is, so please forgive me for not understanding what the temperature is right now. I’m currently on the train form Connecticut back to DC. This hoddle, like Friday, is about a record that meant a lot to me. Today it’s about Fleetwood Mac. They’re one of hte most featured artists in the Track of the Day playlist, but there’s shockingly few of Peter Green. That’s a mistake. I used to work at a running store near Spitafield Market in London. Two days a week the market would have theis assortment of vendors selling their wares: clothing, food, vintage artifacts, etc. I bought a jacket that would last me four years. I also bought Then Play On by Fleetwood Mac. I wanted this one for some time. When I came home that day I played it on my crappy Crossley record player. I loved it. My cope of this album is in rough shape, unfortunately. The album itself plays okay, but the jacket is falling apart. I knew what Peter Green’s Fleetwood Mac was like, but I never listened to this. It’s so far removed from pop, from the standards created by Lindsey Buckingham and Stevie Nicks about a decade later, which would become the version of Fleetwood Mac the world fell in love with. But we should not forget Peter Green. Or Danny Kirwin. This record features some of my favourite Fleetwood Mac songs. Apart from Rumours , it might be my favourite FM piece. Today we’re listening to Closing My Eyes , a gorgeous, bluesy and forlorn piece from Peter Green, whose time with the band would soon be coming to an end. This song hit me like a tonne of bricks when I first played it. Still does. Fitzie’s track of the day: Closing My Eyes, by Fleetwood Mac And now for your links: Your hoddler-in-chief is currently travelling. The commentariat is entrusted to provide its own links.

(Photo by Joshua Gateley/Getty Images) Getty A Los Angeles Clippers commentator and a former NBA player has made a clear statement about Kris Dunn after he was involved in Jalen Williams’ catastrophic injury on Sunday night. Jim Jackson, who played 14 seasons on 12 teams in the NBA, reiterated that Clippers guard Dunn is not a dirty player and should not be misconstrued as the reason why OKC Thunder’s Williams injured his left ankle in a drive late in the fourth quarter. “Kris Dunn is not a dirty player,” he said after the Clippers broadcast the game. “It’s unfortunate that it has happened. We are sending prayers to him and his family and the rest of the organization.” Jim Jackson: "Kris Dunn is not a dirty player" https://t.co/VSrVPKbvi8 pic.twitter.com/tSxGsVlK6q — Oh No He Didn't 🤯 (@ohnohedidnt24) October 26, 2026 What Kris Dunn Did Before Jalen Williams Injury? Getty OKLAHOMA CITY, OKLAHOMA – OCTOBER 25: Jalen Williams #8 of the Oklahoma City Thunder gives a thumbs up to the crowd while being carted off after an injury during the second half against the LA Clippers at Paycom Center on October 25, 2026 in Oklahoma City, Oklahoma. (Photo by Joshua Gateley/Getty Images) Dunn was assessed a flagrant-1 foul following a mid-air contact that resulted in a gruesome, lower-leg injury to Williams. With 1:14 remaining in the fourth quarter, Williams drove toward the basket for a dunk and was sandwiched in mid-air by the LA Clippers defender from behind and Derrick Jones Jr. from the front. The contact from Dunn disrupted Williams’ balance, causing him to fall awkwardly and pin his left leg underneath the full weight of his body. The impact left Williams severely injured, requiring medical staff to place his leg in an air cast and wheel him off the floor on a stretcher while his teammates, especially two-time MVP Shai Gilgeous-Alexander and Chet Holmgren , looked on in visible shock. Gilgeous-Alexander even cried during the post-game interview. The Thunder won the game over the Clippers, 108-101, but a bigger challenge face the team without Williams. Thunder Veteran Shares How Resilient Jalen Williams Is Getty OKLAHOMA CITY, OKLAHOMA – JANUARY 13: Jalen Williams #8 and Alex Caruso #9 of the Oklahoma City Thunder high-five during the second half against the San Antonio Spurs at Paycom Center on January 13, 2026 in Oklahoma City, Oklahoma. (Photo by Joshua Gateley/Getty Images) Thunder veteran Alex Caruso told a story about Jalen Williams’ resilience against any adversity. “(JDub) is a resilient human being. He has great parents, comes from a great family of I think hard work and love and putting your best forward at all times. The couple years I’ve been here, getting to know his mom and dad I know that they raised their children right,” Caruso said after the Clippers game. “And I think those characteristics and qualities are instilled in him as a person. A certain point you can’t be a victim anymore, and you have to take the adversity head on and kind of fight back. And he’s continued to do that, and I know he’ll continue to do it moving forward.” Caruso also talked about the emotions surrounding Williams’ injury, which included those from the Clippers side. “There’s no getting around feeling bad for Dub feeling sorry for him. All the emotions that come with somebody getting stretchered off the court that’s your teammate,” he said. “All the things that he’s been through and the adversity he’s been through to work and get back, and then have something else kind of freak happen to you it stings…it’s just about being there for him and then being professional when it comes to playing basketball. There’s no way to kind of sugarcoat it and get around it and act like you’re not affected by it. You are.” Williams is expected to miss an extended period of time because of the injury. No official diagnosis yet from the team, as of writing. item.title: North Texas star offensive trio teams up for 49-39 win at Navy
item.description: ANNAPOLIS, MD - OCTOBER 24: North Texas running back Jalheim White (1) looks for a opening in the game between the North Texas Mean Green and the Navy Midshipmen on October 24, 2026, at Navy-Marine Corps Memorial Stadium in Annapolis, MD. However, the Mean Green lost all three of those stars in the offseason, forcing the program to start anew offensively. Yet under first-year head coach Neal Brown, a new big three has been established in the program. Tayven Jackson. Jahiem White. Justin Stevenson. North Texas flew into Annapolis for a potential trap game against a Navy offense that found its footing as of late. But thanks to this offensive triumvirate, the Mean Green emerged with their fourth consecutive victory, 49-39, to remain unbeaten in conference play. Jackson recorded 305 passing yards and three touchdowns on a 17-of-23 showing. White rushed for 174 yards and two touchdowns on 20 carries, while adding four receptions for 58 yards. And Stevenson posted a career-high 209 receiving yards on eight receptions and scored twice in the road win. It was a full-fledged offensive shootout in Annapolis as Navy and North Texas combined for 983 yards of total offense, with the Midshipmen creating a slight 506-477 edge. On the home sideline, Jackson Gutierrez kept the Navy offense in the ballgame. The quarterback rushed for 228 yards and three touchdowns — his second 220+ yard, 3-touchdown performance in three weeks — while adding 133 yards and a touchdown through the air. Despite the balanced offensive numbers, the Mean Green won in wire-to-wire fashion and led by as many as 18. North Texas’ defense started the game with a fourth down stop, and that momentum carried over to the offense which created a quick 14-3 lead. It wasn’t just an offensive masterclass. The defense and special teams were responsible for two of North Texas’ seven end zone appearances. Late in the second quarter, the Mean Green utilized some trickery on a punt return in a play inspired by the 2014 St. Louis Rams. Dalton Carnes, who was the gunner in the punt return formation, sprinted back to field the punt, while the designated punt returner Lathan Latiolais was used as a decoy. Navy largely gathered around Latiolais, giving Carnes a free lane down the sideline for a 76-yard touchdown. item.content:encoded: ANNAPOLIS, MD - OCTOBER 24: North Texas running back Jalheim White (1) looks for a opening in the game between the North Texas Mean Green and the Navy Midshipmen on October 24, 2026, at Navy-Marine Corps Memorial Stadium in Annapolis, MD. (Photo by Bradley Rex/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images Last season, North Texas featured the No. 1 passer, No. 5 rusher, and No. 3 receiver in the country. However, the Mean Green lost all three of those stars in the offseason, forcing the program to start anew offensively. Yet under first-year head coach Neal Brown, a new big three has been established in the program. Tayven Jackson. Jahiem White. Justin Stevenson. North Texas flew into Annapolis for a potential trap game against a Navy offense that found its footing as of late. But thanks to this offensive triumvirate, the Mean Green emerged with their fourth consecutive victory, 49-39, to remain unbeaten in conference play. Jackson recorded 305 passing yards and three touchdowns on a 17-of-23 showing. White rushed for 174 yards and two touchdowns on 20 carries, while adding four receptions for 58 yards. And Stevenson posted a career-high 209 receiving yards on eight receptions and scored twice in the road win. It was a full-fledged offensive shootout in Annapolis as Navy and North Texas combined for 983 yards of total offense, with the Midshipmen creating a slight 506-477 edge. On the home sideline, Jackson Gutierrez kept the Navy offense in the ballgame. The quarterback rushed for 228 yards and three touchdowns — his second 220+ yard, 3-touchdown performance in three weeks — while adding 133 yards and a touchdown through the air. Despite the balanced offensive numbers, the Mean Green won in wire-to-wire fashion and led by as many as 18. North Texas’ defense started the game with a fourth down stop, and that momentum carried over to the offense which created a quick 14-3 lead. It wasn’t just an offensive masterclass. The defense and special teams were responsible for two of North Texas’ seven end zone appearances. Late in the second quarter, the Mean Green utilized some trickery on a punt return in a play inspired by the 2014 St. Louis Rams. Dalton Carnes, who was the gunner in the punt return formation, sprinted back to field the punt, while the designated punt returner Lathan Latiolais was used as a decoy. Navy largely gathered around Latiolais, giving Carnes a free lane down the sideline for a 76-yard touchdown. Then in the third quarter, inside linebacker Zakye Barker raced untouched for a 63-yard scoop-and-score to open up a 35-17 lead for the Mean Green. Navy cut the 18-point deficit to three with 10:49 remaining on a Michael Barrow touchdown run, but the one-score margin was short lived. Exactly 71 seconds of game clock later, North Texas reestablished a double-digit advantage on a 59-yard White rushing touchdown — his 11th on the season, which ties him for sixth in the FBS. White then provided the closing efforts, regularly moving the sticks as North Texas used a 12-play drive to consume the final 6:32 of clock. When the Mean Green faced a 4th-and-1 on the possession, Jackson sent a strike to White, who made a spectacular catch to move the team into victory formation. Navy (2-5, 1-4 American) now has as many losses as it did in the two previous seasons combined. Navy is 1-4 in American play, but the Midshipmen have scored at least 30 points in all but one conference matchup this year, as defensive lapses continue to burden the team. Navy takes a brief rest from conference play next week, but that doesn’t mean the competition eases up. The Midshipmen travel to Foxborough, MA for a neutral-site game against perennial rival Notre Dame. North Texas (5-2, 3-0 American) is one of two teams still perfect in American play, sharing the designation with UTSA. The Mean Green overcame a 1-2 start with four consecutive wins, and they have managed at least 44 points in all five victories this season. North Texas finished first nationally in scoring offense last season at 45.1 points per game. Despite a change in the coaching staff and losing every offensive starter, the new-look Mean Green currently rank second in the FBS at 43.1 points per game. The offense looks to continue its dominance Thursday night in Denton, when North Texas plays host to an improved Florida Atlantic team.

item.title: 49ers’ Brock Purdy makes zero injury excuses after turnover fest ruins undefeated season
item.description: Dale Zanine-Imagn Images 49ers’ Brock Purdy makes zero injury excuses after turnover fest ruins undefeated season appeared first on ClutchPoints . Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here . Brock Purdy kept the big picture in focus while acknowledging errors he and the San Francisco 49ers made in their 29-20 loss to the Atlanta Falcons on Sunday afternoon. San Francisco boasted a perfect 6-0 record going into the matchup. The shined as one of the best teams in the league, seeing Purdy play at an elite level. However, they suffered a road upset to the Falcons. They were dealing with injuries as they missed Mike Evans, Deebo Samuel Sr., De’Zhaun Stribling, and Demarcus Robinson within the receiving corps. Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) Purdy reflected on the injuries in the receiving room after the game, per reporter Greg Auman. He gave props to the healthy receivers who stepped up with bigger roles, hoping for the unit to improve with their health amid all the injuries. “With our preparation and how Kyle [Shanahan] goes about the week with getting us ready as an offense and stuff, I think it’s pretty not easy, but he makes it pretty smooth for these guys to come in and learn what they need to do and be on time and all that kind of thing,” Purdy said. “I thought they did a great job today, you know, for what was handed to us and stuff and trying to, you know, we need to limit the turnovers, yes, and we sort of shot ourselves in the foot with that. But you know, the fact that we were out there, you know, having those new guys and stuff out there running routes for us and creating separation and making plays and stuff.” Video: Brock Purdy talks about the injuries at receiver for the 49ers and trying to make plays with newer players pressed into larger roles today. pic.twitter.com/7MMedGDNcO — Greg Auman (@gregauman) October 25, 2026 How Brock Purdy, 49ers played against Falcons Brock Purdy and the 49ers suffered their first loss this season. It was the Falcons’ lucky day as they put an end to San Francisco’s perfect start. Purdy tried his best to get the 49ers back into the game. He completed 27 out of 40 passes for 288 yards and a touchdown and two interceptions. Kaelon Black led the rushing attack with 12 carries for 63 yards and a touchdown. Christian McCaffrey came next with seven rushes for 39 yards and a touchdown while catching six passes for 61 yards. George Kittle topped receivers with eight catches for 88 yards. Meanwhile, Jordan Watkins and Jacob Cowing caught three passes each for 94 yards combined. The 49ers will look to bounce back in their next matchup, being at home. They are on a bye next week before resuming action by hosting the Las Vegas Raiders in Week 9 as kickoff commences on Nov. 8 at 4:05 p.m. ET. Related: 49ers’ Brock Purdy explains brutal blunder that cost San Francisco during Falcons upset Related: 49ers’ Christian McCaffrey returns vs. Falcons after thigh injury scare

item.title: Broncos HC Sean Payton makes admission about playcall that left Jaylen Waddle injured
item.description: Ron Chenoy-Imagn Images Broncos HC Sean Payton makes admission about playcall that left Jaylen Waddle injured appeared first on ClutchPoints . Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here . The Denver Broncos secured an important win over the Arizona Cardinals on Sunday, but Jaylen Waddle ’s late-game injury overshadowed the team’s performance. Meanwhile, Broncos head coach Sean Payton accepted responsibility for a questionable play call that resulted in the wide receiver getting hurt. Payton did not wait for reporters to ask him about the play. Instead, toward the end of his postgame press conference, the Broncos coach addressed his decision himself . “Why didn’t anybody ask me about the dumb reverse call?” Payton said. “It was awful. I’m sorry.” Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) Payton also reflected on a similar mistake he made during his tenure as head coach of the New Orleans Saints, recalling an incident from 2008. “If you look it up in 2008, in a similar situation, even a more radical reverse. Fumbled, Tampa Bay beat us,” Payton added. “I know better. And every once in a while, you fall in love with a play.” The incident occurred with fewer than five minutes remaining in the fourth quarter, when the Broncos were leading by 14 points. Instead of sticking with a conventional offensive approach, Payton called for a reverse designed to get the ball into Waddle’s hands. However, the play quickly went wrong, and the receiver ended up on the ground after attempting to recover a loose ball. Waddle subsequently left the game with a chest injury and did not return. Waddle’s injury was an unwelcome development for Denver, particularly because the receiver had already dealt with chest discomfort during the week leading up to the Cardinals game. He was limited with a chest injury at two practices last week. Waddle’s time in Denver has also been challenging in terms of on-field production . Before exiting the game, he recorded four receptions for 48 yards against the Cardinals. Through seven games this season, he has registered 26 catches for 276 yards and one touchdown. The Broncos will now turn their attention to their Week 8 matchup against the Kansas City Chiefs. Given the circumstances surrounding his exit, Waddle could feature on Denver’s upcoming injury report. Related: Fantasy football managers should take note of Broncos coach Sean Payton’s Jonah Coleman endorsement Related: Broncos’ Bo Nix is just happy to silence ankle injury doubters after 62-yard TD sprint

item.title: Blue Jays predicted to sign $15M former NL wins leader, two-time All-Star to pair with Dylan Cease
item.description: Blue Jays predicted to sign $15M former NL wins leader, two-time All-Star to pair with Dylan Cease originally appeared on The Sporting News . Add The Sporting News as a Preferred Source by clicking here . The Toronto Blue Jays finished one of the most disappointing seasons after competing in the World Series this time a year ago. Toronto never really got going this season, and there are several factors that contributed to its struggles. Injuries were a big part of the problem, especially within the starting rotation. This winter, the Blue Jays will assess which starters are worth pursuing as they prioritize health. “Some injuries, you can see coming. When the 42-year-old Max Scherzer runs into a few IL stints, no one should be surprised. When José Berríos has Tommy John surgery after not missing a start for nearly a decade, it’s terribly unfortunate, but we all understand the realities of baseball and the limitations of the human elbow. The Blue Jays are trying to find that line now between bad luck and controllable variables,” MLB.com’s Keegan Matheson wrote. If spring training rolled around in February, this is what the Blue Jays’ rotation could look like. “So, as long as Cody Ponce is healthy when Opening Day comes around, they will be running a four-man rotation as is: Dylan Cease, Trey Yesavage, Jose Soriano, and Cody Ponce. Eventually, the team will welcome back Jose Berrios, but it has been a rough go of things in terms of his health,” SI’s Maddy Dickens wrote. Toronto could pursue a major starting pitcher this winter. SI’s Zion Trammel believes the Blue Jays could sign Freddy Peralta, who just won the ALCS MVP. “The righty found a groove with Tampa Bay and has dominated the postseason. He's allowed two earned runs and struck out 12 hitters over 16.2 innings. If Peralta continues to excel in the World Series, he will command a competitive market. The Blue could use another starting pitcher, and Peralta would be an excellent addition to the rotation,” Trammel wrote. Peralta has shown his dominance on the biggest stages of October, and there seems to be no one stopping him. Adding another talented arm like Peralta could give the Blue Jays one of baseball’s most formidable rotations when everyone is healthy. Peralta is on a $15 million deal that is set to expire at the conclusion of this season. Toronto is hungry to get back to the World Series, and pursuing Peralta could be a significant move toward achieving that goal. When José Berríos has Tommy John surgery after not missing a start for nearly a decade, it’s terribly unfortunate, but we all understand the realities of baseball and the limitations of the human elbow. The Blue Jays are trying to find that line now between bad luck and controllable variables,” MLB.com’s Keegan Matheson wrote. If spring training rolled around in February, this is what the Blue Jays’ rotation could look like. “So, as long as Cody Ponce is healthy when Opening Day comes around, they will be running a four-man rotation as is: Dylan Cease, Trey Yesavage, Jose Soriano, and Cody Ponce. item.title: Mike Tomlin gets real about Jets’ brutal last two minutes stat under Aaron Glenn
item.description: Vincent Carchietta-Imagn Images Mike Tomlin gets real about Jets’ brutal last two minutes stat under Aaron Glenn appeared first on ClutchPoints . Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here . The New York Jets lost a tough game to the Miami Dolphins on Sunday. New York has now dropped to 2-5 on the 2026 campaign as a result of this defeat. During the game, a brutal stat was made public that further showed how bad things have become. The Jets have been outscored 107-6 in the final two minutes of the first half under Glenn. This is across 24 games. On Sunday, former Pittsburgh Steelers coach Mike Tomlin had quite the reaction to this information. “With three games in, you’ve got enough body of work to determine what your weaknesses are, and then plot out a course to fix them. But they’ve been looking at this particular weakness since the beginning of last season… If I were them, I would do two-minute every day of my life until further notice,” Tomlin said on NBC’s coverage of Sunday Night Football. Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) This troubling trend continued on Sunday against Miami. The Dolphins already had a lead of 14-7 as time ticked away in the first half. Dolphins quarterback Malik Willis then extended the lead to 21-7 with a two-yard rush at the end of the half. New York showed some promise earlier this season. They had close games with the Green Bay Packers and Detroit Lions early on that made it seem like this team may be turning a corner. However, the wins have not followed. On Sunday, they lost to a previously winless Dolphins team that is not close to contention this year. New York has to find ways to turn things around this season. If they don’t, Glenn’s tenure as head coach may end sooner rather than later. The Jets will try to bounce back on November 1 against the Las Vegas Raiders. Related: Jets must end Aaron Glenn era after rock-bottom loss to previously winless Dolphins Related: Jets’ Garrett Wilson already looking forward to ‘feel good’ revenge after losing to Dolphins

item.title: Winners and Losers from Seahawks vs. Chiefs: ‘The Dark Side’ does it again
item.description: The Seattle Seahawks are in the win column again after a complete shutdown of the Kansas City Chiefs offense. While the final score was 20-3 , the game was much more lopsided than that, and better red zone offense would’ve led to an even more emphatic scoreline. Given the San Francisco 49ers loss earlier in the day, this was a massive opportunity for the Seahawks to get back into the NFC West race and turn their season around. They took full advantage and reminded everyone that when they keep the mistakes to a minimum, they’re still one of the NFL’s best. Let’s get to Winners and Losers! Seattle Seahawks Winners There’s nobody better at wide receiver right now than Jaxon Smith-Njigba Could I lead with anybody else? By halftime he had 6 catches for 129 yards and a touchdown, and it really should’ve been 8/142/1 if not for a couple of screens that were thrown as laterals. His final stat-line was 9/150/1 to continue his outrageous follow-up season to his Offensive Player of the Year 2025 season. We will soon be talking about JSN not just as one of the best receivers in the NFL, but one of the best receivers to have ever played the game. And in an ideal world, he’ll spend every single one of those seasons as a Seattle Seahawk. Emanuel Wilson grinds out a workmanlike 100-yard performance If Kenneth Walker not getting 100 yards (or really being all that effective at all) was not some earth-shattering surprise going up against the vaunted Seattle run defense, who had Emanuel Wilson going for 100? The bulk of his bulldozing came in the fourth quarter when the Chiefs defense was worn out and Wilson had time to work. His 21-yard touchdown run gives him his fourth overall TD on the year, and he’s well on pace to set a career high in rushing yards. Wilson’s role is simple: north-south, physical runner who can give you some help as a receiving back. He’s not flashy but he’s a playable back with the right blocking and right play-calls. When Zach Charbonnet and Jadarian Price return, Wilson should still get some touches. Sam Darnold, even with the interception, played very well By the time I hit publish on this article I will be under the covers and snoring my life away. I fully expect some dissenting voices as far as putting Sam on the Winners list because of how bad that end zone interception was. There’s no excusing the pick, but it was also more or less the only blemish on a highly efficient night. He got the ball out quickly, on time, and accurately. He scrambled for critical first downs, didn’t take any sacks, and outside of the pick he also wasn’t forcing doomed passes into tight coverage. Darnold looked comfortable and in control of the offense almost all night, and his deep balls to Jaxon Smith-Njigba were a thing of beauty to watch. I can live with Darnold’s brain cramps when he’s largely productive and playing winning football. It’s the preceding two weeks in which Darnold becomes a liability more than the solution. item.content:encoded: The Seattle Seahawks are in the win column again after a complete shutdown of the Kansas City Chiefs offense. While the final score was 20-3 , the game was much more lopsided than that, and better red zone offense would’ve led to an even more emphatic scoreline. Given the San Francisco 49ers loss earlier in the day, this was a massive opportunity for the Seahawks to get back into the NFC West race and turn their season around. They took full advantage and reminded everyone that when they keep the mistakes to a minimum, they’re still one of the NFL’s best. Let’s get to Winners and Losers! Seattle Seahawks Winners There’s nobody better at wide receiver right now than Jaxon Smith-Njigba Could I lead with anybody else? By halftime he had 6 catches for 129 yards and a touchdown, and it really should’ve been 8/142/1 if not for a couple of screens that were thrown as laterals. His final stat-line was 9/150/1 to continue his outrageous follow-up season to his Offensive Player of the Year 2025 season. We will soon be talking about JSN not just as one of the best receivers in the NFL, but one of the best receivers to have ever played the game. And in an ideal world, he’ll spend every single one of those seasons as a Seattle Seahawk. Emanuel Wilson grinds out a workmanlike 100-yard performance If Kenneth Walker not getting 100 yards (or really being all that effective at all) was not some earth-shattering surprise going up against the vaunted Seattle run defense, who had Emanuel Wilson going for 100? The bulk of his bulldozing came in the fourth quarter when the Chiefs defense was worn out and Wilson had time to work. His 21-yard touchdown run gives him his fourth overall TD on the year, and he’s well on pace to set a career high in rushing yards. Wilson’s role is simple: north-south, physical runner who can give you some help as a receiving back. He’s not flashy but he’s a playable back with the right blocking and right play-calls. When Zach Charbonnet and Jadarian Price return, Wilson should still get some touches. Sam Darnold, even with the interception, played very well By the time I hit publish on this article I will be under the covers and snoring my life away. I fully expect some dissenting voices as far as putting Sam on the Winners list because of how bad that end zone interception was. There’s no excusing the pick, but it was also more or less the only blemish on a highly efficient night. He got the ball out quickly, on time, and accurately. He scrambled for critical first downs, didn’t take any sacks, and outside of the pick he also wasn’t forcing doomed passes into tight coverage. Darnold looked comfortable and in control of the offense almost all night, and his deep balls to Jaxon Smith-Njigba were a thing of beauty to watch. I can live with Darnold’s brain cramps when he’s largely productive and playing winning football. It’s the preceding two weeks in which Darnold becomes a liability more than the solution. Tonight, Darnold looked a lot more like 2025 Darnold, and he did so against a Steve Spagnuolo defense. Brian Fleury (somewhat) quiets the critics Speaking of Seahawks under fire, Brian Fleury needed the offense to look cohesive and functional. I won’t pretend it’s perfect and I won’t pretend it’s optimal to constantly have to convert third and medium or long, but would you rather they show they can convert in obvious passing situations or not? I thought so. Fleury had answers for situations in which the offense had struggled, and he outfoxed Spags. A lot of the offensive woes have been poor player execution, but I don’t think Fleury has put the Seahawks in the best positions to succeed. He did a much better job settling Sam Darnold early, using play-action more efficiently even in lower volume, and using the run game to help limit the possessions in the game. Kansas City had few opportunities to respond, whereas the Seahawks did enough with their possessions. There’s still a lot to work on as far as getting plays in quicker and not short-circuiting in the low red zone, but I was very happy with the flow of the game. Perhaps that mini-bye was the breather Fleury and Sam needed to figure some things out. I’m eager to see if this is more than a one-off and the start of legitimate improvement after a rocky start. stuff @TheHawksEyePod has been talking about, but off the broadcast it felt like on the deeper drops the progression within their common concepts was adapted to the coverage more or at least Sam was finding those windows way earlier. Basically, They Got Good. https://t.co/cl3m6HZYp6 — under zone x (@cmikesspinmove) October 26, 2026 George Holani did some dirty work you’ll appreciate later Holani had a pivotal third down conversion when he broke two tackles on a checkdown. That’s not the play I want to focus on. Holani had a key block on Darnold’s second scramble for a first down, but he also slowed down Nohl Williams on the interception runback, which allowed Charles Cross to make the tackle. In effect, Holani helped save at least a touchdown and assured the Chiefs could only muster up a long field goal attempt (which was missed). That’s winning football. That’s 12 as One. Holani didn’t wow with his touches outside of his catch, but he won in the margins when he didn’t have the ball. A.J. Barner gets more involved You wanted the Barnyard? You got it three times and it worked every time. Barner also had four catches for 42 yards, so he finally was more involved in the passing game as a receiving threat. He was a tipped ball away from probably scoring a touchdown in the second quarter. Happy National Tight Ends Day, A.J! The offensive line did its job and then some No sacks, only two quarterback hits allowed, and zero holding penalties. Anthony Bradford coming back provided some stabilization if only for communication purposes, not necessarily blocking performance in itself. This was a tough assignment dealing with Chris Jones and George Karlaftis while facing Spags’ blitzes, and the Seahawks OL won the challenge. Nick Emmanwori is a monster I don’t think Emmanwori has played a better game in his young career than Sunday night. He hassled Mahomes into an interception, covered Xavier Worthy down the field, played the run well, he did everything you’d want out of your Apex superstar. There were a couple of times he was caught out of position on an improvised Mahomes scramble to a tight end, but Mahomes does that to everyone. If Emmanwori had some sort of hip thing before this game that led to a questionable designation, he could’ve fooled me in terms of how healthy he looked. Emmanwori must love synth-pop because he was in full Erasure mode tonight . Ty Okada lives for Sunday nights To date, Okada has two career interceptions. Both have come in spectacular fashion on SNF. Seattle has undeniably had issues replacing the depth they lost at edge and running back, but Coby Bryant’s exit has stung far less because Okada (and Rodney Thomas II when Ty was injured) is a more than capable starting safety. Tyrice Knight continues filling in nicely for Drake Thomas The first play of the game, T-Knight got juked out by Kenneth Walker. He had Walker in his hip pocket the remainder of the night, closing up holes and doing an exemplary job with his run fits throughout the night. Seattle’s linebacker depth was once a question mark at the start of 2025 (outside of Ernest Jones IV, of course). It is now a position of quiet strength. Derick Hall leads the pass rush Whew! I’ve been harsh on Seattle’s edge group for not being productive enough, but after a slow start the Seahawks edges capitalized on Kansas City’s backup tackles. Hall was outstanding and recorded a strip sack, plus he had several pressures. Hell, even Dante Fowler Jr was doing stuff! Mahomes was sacked just once but you could feel that DeMarcus Lawrence, Hall, Uchenna Nwosu, and Fowler were speeding Patrick up. Leonard Williams and Byron Murphy dominate Want

item.title: “Our Crap Stinks”: Mike Brown Blasts Knicks as Jalen Brunson Sends Important Locker Room Message to Teammates
item.description: March 9, 2026, Inglewood, California, USA: Head coach, Mike Brown of the New York Knicks gives instructions during a time out in a 2026 NBA, Basketball Herren, USA regular season game against the LA Clippers on Monday March 9, 2026 at Intuit Dome Arena in Inglewood, California. JAVIER ROJAS/PI Inglewood USA – ZUMAp124 20260309_zaa_p124_015 Copyright: xJavierxRojasx ©Credit - Imago Three games into the new season, and the defending champion New York Knicks are still searching for their first victory. Sunday night’s 111-102 defeat against the Orlando Magic at Madison Square Garden marked their third straight loss. A terrible fourth-quarter collapse left the home crowd in silence, watching a team that looks completely different from the squad that won it all just a few months ago. Inside the press room, head coach Mike Brown did not hold back his anger. A few doors down in the locker room, captain Jalen Brunson took a calmer path, calling on his teammates to stay united before this early crisis gets out of hand. “The biggest thing is to continue to coach them and/or tell them the truth,” Brown said during his post-game media session . He insisted that championship rings from last season do not guarantee easy wins today. “When we play well, like I told them just now, I said, ‘Hey, we were great transition in the second half.’ You know, we were. But now we got to continue trying to embrace the little things, and we got to make sure we’re doing it in practice so it has carryover into the game. I mean, I’ll really jump their a– if I see the effort not there. You know, because to me that’s a whole different thing.” The Knicks are in crisis mode with their coach delivering brutal criticism and their star point guard rallying the locker room. Subscribe to stay on top of this pivotal moment in New York's season. JAVIER ROJAS/PI Inglewood USA – ZUMAp124 20260309_zaa_p124_015 Copyright: xJavierxRojasx ©Credit - Imago Three games into the new season, and the defending champion New York Knicks are still searching for their first victory. Sunday night’s 111-102 defeat against the Orlando Magic at Madison Square Garden marked their third straight loss. A terrible fourth-quarter collapse left the home crowd in silence, watching a team that looks completely different from the squad that won it all just a few months ago. Inside the press room, head coach Mike Brown did not hold back his anger. A few doors down in the locker room, captain Jalen Brunson took a calmer path, calling on his teammates to stay united before this early crisis gets out of hand. “The biggest thing is to continue to coach them and/or tell them the truth,” Brown said during his post-game media session . He insisted that championship rings from last season do not guarantee easy wins today. “When we play well, like I told them just now, I said, ‘Hey, we were great transition in the second half.’ You know, we were. But now we got to continue trying to embrace the little things, and we got to make sure we’re doing it in practice so it has carryover into the game. I mean, I’ll really jump their a– if I see the effort not there. You know, because to me that’s a whole different thing.” The Knicks are in crisis mode with their coach delivering brutal criticism and their star point guard rallying the locker room. Subscribe to stay on top of this pivotal moment in New York's season. Credits: Imagn Brown then delivered the direct reality check that caught everyone’s attention. “If we’re trying and trying the right way, sometimes you got to fight through stuff like this to get yourself on track. But games like this will tell us that, like I said before, our crap stinks. You know, it does. And we’re the only ones that can do something about it. There’s no light switch that we can just turn on and think we’re gonna go win ballgames. Nobody’s gonna give us anything. So we have to be better with the little things until we start shooting the ball well.” Mike Brown highlighted the little things that need fine-tuning. It’s something that even Jalen Brunson addressed later. Brown’s anger was fully justified by what happened on the floor. The Knicks held a 10-point lead heading into the fourth quarter, with 9 minutes and 20 seconds remaining, only to surrender 40 points at the end while committing eight costly turnovers. Orlando outran and outworked New York when the game was on the line. Away from the cameras, Jalen Brunson gathered the group for a captain’s talk. “Control what you can control; focus on the little details that may seem small but are going to impact winning. Most importantly, let’s do it together. One thing I’ve said throughout the entire training camp, and honestly to this day, is we’re going to see who we are within the first couple of weeks of the season. So we’re hitting adversity now and happy good from.” The defeat was not an isolated late-game failure. T he Knicks also lost to Philadelphia and Boston to open the season , leaving the reigning champions at 0-3. They are the first defending NBA champions to begin a season with three consecutive losses since the 2011-12 Dallas Mavericks. Behind the scenes, the early struggles are not completely shocking. After a few offseason roster tweaks and adjusting to new rotation pieces, New York is still trying to find its defensive identity. Chemistry takes time to click, even for champions, but three games of blown leads prove that the learning curve is steeper than most people and the players expected. Even with the collapse, the team did show flashes of offensive rhythm. The big three combined for 72 points, and that kind of firepower is something the Knicks will lean on heavily through the long grind of the regular season. If New York drops Tuesday’s game and slips to 0-4, the early panic button in the locker room will turn into real pressure from the front office. A slow start in a brutal Eastern Conference means every blown lead now could come back to haunt their playoff seeding down the road. item.title: LAFC clinches playoff berth, but can the roller coaster season level out?
item.description: Armindo Seib #9 of LAFC celebrates after giving an assist during an MLS regular season match against LA Galaxy on October 25, 2026 at BMO Stadium in Los Angeles, California. LOS ANGELES --- An 11-game unbeaten streak to begin 2026. Only three wins out of the next 12 before heading into the World Cup break. A fired head coach in late September. Now, four games without a loss since. It's safe to say that LAFC has had quite a roller coaster of a season. Yet, despite all the chaos, a 2-2 draw against the LA Galaxy on Saturday night at BMO Stadium was enough to clinch a spot in the MLS Cup Playoffs for the eighth time in nine years. Just two games remain in the regular season, with the Black & Gold sitting 12-9-11 and sixth in the Western Conference (47 points). Although time is limited, there's still an opportunity for LA to climb into the top four and secure home-field advantage in their Round One match. Fourth-place San Jose and fifth-place Houston both hold only a slim one-point advantage. It's certainly fair to critique, however, that LAFC should never have found itself this far down the table in the first place. Start with the 11-game unbeaten run, which gave glimpses of a team that looked as if it could run away with the conference. Then came the dip. Three wins in 12 matches before the World Cup break turned a commanding position into a scramble, and the club never managed to fully recover its early-season identity. By the time Marc Dos Santos was fired on Sept. 27, the question was much less about whether LAFC could contend for the top seed, but rather if it could stabilize at all. This is what makes its recent stretch notable. Four games without a loss under interim head coach Xavi Tamarit won't erase a rough middle of the season, but they have given the group something it lacked for months. Although three of those four results have been draws, they've provided a sense of direction. And Saturday night, against its crosstown rival, Tamarit was sure to credit the supporters as much as his own players. "The fans...we were losing two to zero, and the fans were supporting and pushing us a lot," he said. "We play with the heart of the people, and I congratulate the team because this is the team we want to see in the future." Tamarit was also quick to put the team's accomplishment in perspective. "I'm really happy to be in the playoffs. The club, the players, all of us, we fight for that, and I think we have to be happy because it's not easy for anyone." It's a fair response considering the big picture. Making the playoffs in eight of nine years is the sort of consistency that most clubs envy, even in a season this rocky. Defender Aaron Long believes that LAFC's display of resilience on Saturday is indicative of the team's identity. "I think we're a dangerous team," he said. "I think we're a team that is showing that we're willing to fight even in tough moments." That willingness to fight has often been embodied by the Black & Gold's all-time leadi

Although three of those four results have been draws, they've provided a sense of direction. "The fans...we were losing two to zero, and the fans were supporting and pushing us a lot," he said. "We play with the heart of the people, and I congratulate the team because this is the team we want to see in the future." Tamarit was also quick to put the team's accomplishment in perspective. "I'm really happy to be in the playoffs. The club, the players, all of us, we fight for that, and I think we have to be happy because it's not easy for anyone." It's a fair response considering the big picture. Making the playoffs in eight of nine years is the sort of consistency that most clubs envy, even in a season this rocky. Defender Aaron Long believes that LAFC's display of resilience on Saturday is indicative of the team's identity. "I think we're a dangerous team," he said. "I think we're a team that is showing that we're willing to fight even in tough moments." That willingness to fight has often been embodied by the Black & Gold's all-time leading scorer, Denis Bouanga, who once again found himself at the center of the action against the Galaxy. He's now scored against them in eight consecutive meetings, and his 12 goals in 11 battles against the club match former LAFC great Carlos Vela for the most in the series' history. Those numbers alone would make for a memorable evening, but they aren't even the most impressive part of his résumé. Bouanga is now just two goals shy of becoming the only player in MLS history to score 20 goals in four consecutive seasons. Yet, individual milestones aren't where his satisfaction lies. "Honestly, I don't care individually because the last three seasons I completed everything individually, but nothing with the team," Bouanga said. "That's why I'm so mad sometimes." That frustration is understandable. He was part of the 2022 squad that lifted the MLS Cup, so he knows what the finish line feels like. But for all of his production since, he hasn't been able to pair his numbers with another desperately coveted title. This postseason provides his next chance to change that, and his belief in the group hasn't wavered. Denis Bouanga #99 of LAFC reacts after a VAR review during an MLS regular season match against LA Galaxy on October 25, 2026 at BMO Stadium in Los Angeles, California. Steven Park - The Sporting Tribune Denis Bouanga #99 of LAFC reacts after a VAR review during an MLS regular season match against LA Galaxy on October 25, 2026 at BMO Stadium in Los Angeles, California. "We can do something for sure. Some teams don't want to play against us." Bouanga may be right, but belief alone, of course, won't be enough. The inconsistency that defined LAFC's season must continue to be addressed in the final two games, particularly if the club hopes to climb past Houston and San Jose to secure home-field advantage in the opening round. If not, LA will need to search for comfort on the road, where playoff soccer can see a single mistake lead to drastic damage. Defensive lapses, like the ones that put the team at a two-goal deficit against the Galaxy, can't be tolerated in such a high-stakes setting. It doesn't help, either, that the Black & Gold have just three wins in 16 tries on the road so far this season. Still, there are reasons for optimism. The team has managed to curb its losses under Tamarit. Bouanga and Son Heung-min, the other half of LA's prolific playmaking duo, are playing like they have something to prove. Son's 15 assists are tied for the league lead. Bouanga's 27 goal contributions leave him second in MLS behind only Lionel Messi. A roller coaster season doesn't always have to end with a crash at the bottom. If LAFC can finally level out, this one might just have one last climb in it.

item.title: Braves predicted to sign 39-HR slugger, Triple Crown winner to fill void left by Jurickson Profar
item.description: Braves predicted to sign 39-HR slugger, Triple Crown winner to fill void left by Jurickson Profar originally appeared on The Sporting News . Add The Sporting News as a Preferred Source by clicking here . The Atlanta Braves are heading into another interesting offseason as they determine which areas need the most attention and which ones require less work. Obviously, the starting rotation needs attention, and the outfield could use some help as well. Left field has been a problem for the last two seasons, largely because of Jurickson Profar. He has been suspended in each of his first two years with Atlanta. “Atlanta Braves designated hitter Jurickson Profar is facing a 162-game suspension after testing positive for a performance-enhancing drug for the second time in the last year, sources told ESPN on Tuesday. Profar, 33, is the sixth player to receive a 162-game ban for PED use since Major League Baseball increased the penalty for two-time offenders to a full season in 2014. He will forfeit the entirety of his $15 million salary," ESPN's Jeff Passan wrote. The Braves tried to give Lane Thomas some playing time in left field after the trade deadline, but it didn’t go as planned. “The Braves acquired outfielder Lane Thomas and minor league left-hander Bailey Falter from the Royals in exchange for two minor league pitchers Saturday. Thomas, 30, is slashing .232/.326/.393 in 97 games with the Royals this year. He has played mostly center field in Kansas City but will move over to left field in Atlanta and likely platoon with Mike Yastrzemski. Thomas is a career .288 hitter against left-handed pitching," ESPN wrote. The outfield still needs help, especially in the form of another bat. SI’s Harrison Smajovitts believes the Braves should sign Japanese star Teruaki Sato. “He can also play in the outfield, with 262 games played at the position in the NPB. It's his primary position, that's third base (more on that momentarily), but it's not a position that he's only tried out a handful of times. Upon arrival, Sato will be one of their top left-handed bats alongside Drake Baldwin and Michael Harris II. Beyond them, the Braves' best left-handed bat who isn't a switch hitter is Mike Yastrzemski. Sato is an everyday player, not just someone whose job is to bash righties. However, having that extra left-handed bat could do wonders,” Smajovitts wrote. Sato could be used as an outfield option in left field or potentially right field when Ronald Acuña Jr. gets a day off. He would be a great pickup, as Sato is a Triple Crown winner. Sato also hit 39 home runs last season, so the power is clearly there. Atlanta needs someone who can provide stability in left field, and Sato could bring exactly that to the table. The Braves need this type of player to strengthen their lineup and improve their outfield production. item.title: Kevin O’Connell insists Vikings’ offense is close to breaking out despite another lifeless showing
item.description: Brad Rempel-Imagn Images Kevin O’Connell insists Vikings’ offense is close to breaking out despite another lifeless showing appeared first on ClutchPoints . Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here . As the adage goes, defense wins championships. Surely, the Minnesota Vikings would like to believe so. The defense stepped up anew as the Vikings escaped the Indianapolis Colts , 16-10, at US Bank Stadium, keeping them undefeated at 6-0. Harrison Smith picked off Daniel Jones’ pass in the final minute to seal the victory. It was a fitting end, with the Vikings relying on their defense for the majority of the contest. The team’s woes on offense were highlighted again, but coach Kevin O’Connell maintained an optimistic view , as reported by ESPN’s Kevin Seifert. Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) “There were nine explosive (plays) on offense, but we left a lot out there. I think our guys are very confident that we’re not far off. The ‘far off’ changes a little bit as you go, but I’m very, very confident we’ll get it going,” said O’Connell. Kyler Murray went 14-of-24 for 150 yards and one touchdown. Jordan Jefferson had 15 carries for 68 yards, while Justin Jefferson and TJ Hockenson combined for eight receptions and 79 yards. Hockenson scored a touchdown. The Vikings have allowed only 12.8 points per game, the stingiest in the NFL. They, however, only have 10 touchdowns in six games. Murray had a similar view as O’Connell regarding their offense. “We’ll continue to get better. I know we will. I know we keep saying that, but I felt like we moved the ball well today. We’ve just got to put the ball in the end zone,” said Murray, who is in his first season with Minnesota. The Vikings will visit the Detroit Lions in Week 8. Related: Vikings’ Brian Flores keeps breaking his own records with mind-boggling blitz numbers Related: Vikings are 6-0 with 1 of worst offenses in NFL after defense, special teams magic does it again

item.title: ‘Rams Are Feeling Pretty Good About Their Chances’ — Giants Legend on Los Angeles’ Playoff Hopes After ‘Do-or-Die’ Win Over Raiders
item.description: Oct 25, 2026; Paradise, Nevada, USA; Los Angeles Rams quarterback Matthew Stafford (9) practices before the game at Allegiant Stadium. © David Brytus-Imagn Images The Los Angeles Rams are back in the win column after a convincing 35-21 victory over the Las Vegas Raiders in Week 7. They snapped their two-game losing streak and improved to 3-4 on the season. The win was crucial, as another loss would have put their playoff hopes in serious jeopardy, although it is still too early to make any definitive predictions. Quarterback Matthew Stafford and the offense delivered when it mattered most. The running back duo of Blake Corum and Kyren Williams made all the difference on the ground, while Stafford broke the franchise record for career touchdown passes. Hall of Famer Michael Strahan believes the Rams are in a good spot, but need to be careful with their approach. Giants Legend Drops His Reaction to Rams’ Win Over the Raiders In Week 7, the San Francisco 49ers lost to the Atlanta Falcons, while the Arizona Cardinals fell to the Denver Broncos. These results helped the Rams climb from the bottom of the NFC West standings, moving them to third place in the division. During Fox’s Week 7 recap, Rob Gronkowski and Strahan shared their thoughts on the Rams’ win and what the team needs to do moving forward. BE THE GM OF YOUR FAVORITE TEAM: PFN’s Free NFL Mock Draft Simulator “If you’re the Rams, you’re just hoping that you just keep it close, hang in there,” Strahan said on Sunday night. “Keep it close. Get through the injuries. And today was a big win for them. This was a do-or-die win. They lose this game today, I think they’re completely out of it. But I think because of the San Francisco loss and Seattle having a tough contest tonight, the Rams are feeling pretty good about their chances to stay in there,” he added. Gronkowski also credited the Rams’ running backs for their dominance on the ground. Corum and Williams combined for 33 carries and came close to breaching the 200-yard mark. “This is the Rams that we expected to see from the beginning of the year. If they can continue this and keep it going, yes, they can turn around the season,” he said on the show. SET YOUR LINEUPS: PFN’s Free Fantasy Start/Sit Optimizer Stafford also made headlines, throwing three touchdown passes to reach 155 in a Rams uniform, surpassing Roman Gabriel’s franchise record of 154. He finished 23-of-29 for 195 yards with an 82.2 PFN QB Impact Grade , good enough for sixth this week. Although he threw an interception, his efficiency and the run game made all the difference. The Rams are currently ranked No. 16 in PFN’s NFL Team Impact Rankings . Next up, they play the only winless team in the NFL, the 0-6 Los Angeles Chargers, in Week 8. The game is scheduled for a 4:05 p.m. ET kickoff at SoFi Stadium on November 1, 2026. This article originally appeared on Pro Football Network .

item.title: ‘Embarrassing,’ ‘Serious Wake-Up Call’ — Concerns Mount As Defending NBA Champion Knicks Make Unwanted History With Disastrous 0-3 Start
item.description: 'Embarrassing,' 'Serious Wake-Up Call' -- Concerns Mount As Defending NBA Champion Knicks Make Unwanted History With Disastrous 0-3 Start As the great Yogi Berra once said, “It gets late early out there.” The same goes for the 0-3 New York Knicks after the Orlando Magic outworked them at home without their best player, Paolo Banchero (ankle). The Knicks became the first defending NBA champions since 2011 to start 0-3, and just the third all-time. In a talented Eastern Conference, they can’t afford to slide much farther, as worries mount. Fans Voice Growing Concerns As Winless Knicks Make Dubious History It’s unclear whether the Knicks are suffering a mental hangover from their championship, some kind of malaise, or a potential roster deficiency. Perhaps it’s all of the above, but the wider NBA community is wondering what is going on inside Madison Square Garden. NBA insider Brett Siegel pointed out New York’s unwanted history on Sunday: “The Knicks are the first defending champions since the Mavericks in 2011 to lose each of their first three games of the new season. Dallas went on to lose in the first round of the playoffs that year as the defending champions.” Legion Hoops also posted a remarkable graphic, tweeting: “The two most expensive rosters in the NBA haven’t gotten a win yet this season.” The Golden State Warriors and the Knicks are both winless with a combined payroll of $452 million. Furthermore, the Giannis Antetokounmpo-led Miami Heat are also 0-3, adding to the surprising early-season struggles of some of the league’s highest-profile teams. New York fan account KnicksMuse rejected excuses and called the 0-3 start “quite embarrassing.” That sentiment was also echoed by Knicks Nation, who tweeted, “Don’t think I had the Knicks opening the season 0-3. Tonight was pretty embarrassing.” NBA content creator Six Rings of Steel called out Jalen Brunson and Mikal Bridges, saying both need to be better, and concluded: “Championship hangover in full effect right now.” ESPN’s Sam Block tweeted similarly: “The championship hangover is real.” Dylan Backer, head of content at Empire Sports Media, astutely described the situation: “Incredible meltdown by the Knicks. They aren’t this bad, but they sure are playing like they are.” CBS Sports reporter and Knicks fan Ashley Nicole Moss added that the winless start “needs to be a SERIOUS wake-up call for this team.” A wake-up call appears to be urgently needed, as Orlando outhustled New York and set the tempo. The Magic had more rebounds (49-45) and assists (29-26) and nearly double the points off turnovers (23-12) as they overcame a double-digit fourth-quarter deficit. The Knicks’ transition defense has also been missing in all three games; on Sunday, they allowed 18 3-pointers, many from transition 3s. MORE: ‘Grass Ain’t Greener On the Other Side,’ ‘Wasting Another Year’ — NBA World Reacts to Giannis Antetokounmpo’s Frustration Amid Heat’s Alarming 0-3 Start Offensively, Brunson continues to struggle

MORE: ‘Grass Ain’t Greener On the Other Side,’ ‘Wasting Another Year’ — NBA World Reacts to Giannis Antetokounmpo’s Frustration Amid Heat’s Alarming 0-3 Start Offensively, Brunson continues to struggle, shooting 39.1% overall and 26.7% from deep. Meanwhile, Bridges has been a nonfactor; he followed his previous 0-point effort with just 6 points and is shooting a jarring 0% from long range for the season. Essentially, the only player in the rotation who looks ready to play is Karl-Anthony Towns. The star big man is averaging 21.0 points and 12.0 rebounds while shooting 62.2% from the field. His teammates, especially Brunson, may need to feed him the ball and make him the focal point of the attack, at least until the starters return to their usual form. This is a prideful, extremely talented, and hard-working group, so they should turn it around, but it has to start here. It won’t get any easier, however, as New York faces the unbeaten Detroit Pistons (3-0) next. This article originally appeared on Pro Football Network .

item.title: Devils win 4-2 at Panthers to boost cup bid
item.description: The 4-2 win at Nottingham Panthers was Cardiff Devils first win on the road this season [Nottingham Panthers] Cardiff Devils are guaranteed at least an elimination game for the Challenge Cup semi-finals, after a hard-earned win at Nottingham Panthers. The Welsh club top the standings after a 4-2 victory in their penultimate game of an incredibly tight Group A - with five teams still hoping to progress. Nick Welsh put the visitors in front in the opening period with Evan Mosey doubling their advantage in the second, before two goals in a minute from Panthers Aiden Hansen-Bukata and Spencer Naas tied the game. Nolan Yaremko quickly restored Cardiff's lead, and in a tense third period Ryan Barrow sealed victory with an empty-net goal seven seconds from the end. "It was a must-win game for us tonight, we didn't want to leave it to chance with that last game and others playing before us," said Mosey, who was icing for the first time since injuring a knee in September's home tie against Panthers. "We had a job to do. The boys played unbelievably," added the 37-year-old. Sunday's results left four sides - Cardiff, Sheffield Steelers, Panthers and Guildford Flames - all on 12 points. Manchester Storm in fifth, with seven points, could also make the knockout stages having three games still to play. Guildford in third place and Nottingham in fourth have both completed their 10-game programme, while Steelers - beaten 1-0 in Cardiff on Saturday - and the Devils both have one match to play. Sheffield host Storm on Wednesday, 28 October, before the Manchester side welcome bottom club Coventry Blaze on Friday, 30 October and Cardiff on Sunday, 1 November. The top two sides in Group A automatically qualify for the semi-final, with the third-placed team facing an elimination tie against the runners-up in the smaller group B. Belfast Giants have already secured their place in the last four as winners of that group, while with three games each to play, Fife Flyers are second three points clear of Glasgow Clan and four ahead of Dundee Stars. GB men and women to make history in Glasgow

item.title: Devonte Wyatt Blasts Officials After Controversial Late-Game Penalty
item.description: GREEN BAY, WISCONSIN - OCTOBER 11: Devonte Wyatt #95 of the Green Bay Packers looks on during the game against the Chicago Bears at Lambeau Field on October 11, 2026 in Green Bay, Wisconsin. (Photo by Daniel Bartel/Getty Images) Getty Green Bay Packers defensive tackle Devonte Wyatt got hit with a very controversial late unnecessary roughness penalty late during a tackle on Amon-Ra St. Brown that accidentally caused the referee to fall down. This gave the Lions a first down on the Packers 11, which ultimately lead to a Detroit touchdown. Whilst fans were up-in-arms at the situation, no one spoke out more defiantly in defense of his own play than Wyatt, who ripped into the referees post-game for their decision-making on the field. Devonte Wyatt Speaks Out on Unnecessary Roughness Penalty Packers DT Devonte Wyatt on his penalty: "If you asked me right now, I’d do the same thing 100 times over. So that’s the refs. They gotta figure out what they need to do because I definitely did my job." — Rob Demovsky (@RobDemovsky) October 26, 2026 Devonte Wyatt to @RobDemovsky : "What if (St. Brown) would’ve got up and ran for a touchdown? Then everybody would be looking at D-Wy like, ‘You let him go’ … I feel like the refs were on their side the whole day." "If it wasn’t for the flags, we would’ve won that game." — Matt Schneidman (@mattschneidman) October 26, 2026 “If you asked me right now, I’d do the same thing 100 times over. So that’s the refs. They gotta figure out what they need to do because I definitely did my job.” Wyatt said to ESPN’s Rob Demovsky. “What if (St. Brown) would’ve got up and ran for a touchdown?” Wyatt continued. “Then everybody would be looking at D-Wy like, ‘You let him go’ … I feel like the refs were on their side the whole day… If it wasn’t for the flags, we would’ve won that game.” Wyatt Penalty Had Major Impact in Packers Loss Wyatt protested that he was simply ensuring Amon-Ra St.Brown was fully down after the tackle, whereas the referees claimed that the former first round DT was continuing the play after the whistle had gone; a whistle that Wyatt claims he never heard. That was a legitimate turning point in the game. And whilst it was by far the only route to victory for Green Bay; kicker Trey Smack missed two very make-able field goals in the first and fourth and fourth quarters; it certainly could have shifted the balance of the game late on. The Packers move to 4-3 on the season, half a game behind the Lions at 4-2, and 2.5 games behind division leaders the Minnesota Vikings at 6-0. item.title: Fernando Alonso blasts driving standards of bottom half of F1 grid
item.description: Motorsport photo Fernando Alonso let rip at Williams' Alex Albon after contact between their cars on the opening lap of the Formula 1 United States Grand Prix. It cost the Aston Martin driver four places in Austin and left him with floor damage, which compromised the AMR26 for the rest of the race. The two-time world champion lost one position at the start from 12th on the grid as Esteban Ocon surged from 15th to 11th. Albon picked up three places with a clean launch to run 14th and challenged Alonso for position all the way through the Esses on the opening lap. At Turn 11, Alonso made a bid to pass the squabbling Haas cars on the inside line into the left-hander, but Albon had also launched on a similar trajectory. The Williams was already committed as the gap narrowed, and Albon's front-right wheel crunched into Alonso's left-hand bargeboard and floor edge. Alonso was pushed onto the outside kerb, losing a further four places. The damage to the Aston Martin's floor was clearly visible from Albon's on-board camera. Alonso recovered to 12th place at the chequered flag, but was clearly disgruntled when he spoke to the media. "That was the biggest damage," he said. "I think we lost half a second or more [per lap]. The car is destroyed; I saw it in parc ferme. Half of the floor is not there. I don't know how we kept on going and how we were semi-competitive. "I imagine if the car was in one piece, probably today the points were a strong possibility because we were running P12 with half a car. I lost even further pieces of the floor. I couldn't turn. So we stopped. I thought about retiring the car. I was ready to switch it off. Alexander Albon, Williams, Fernando Alonso, Aston Martin Racing Alexander Albon, Williams, Fernando Alonso, Aston Martin Racing "But then they put a new front wing and I went out again. Obviously the car was turning ok to the right and not ok to the left for the last 15 laps of the race. But we wanted to finish and collect a little bit more data. "When you start at the back, there is this risk always. I think the quality of the drivers in the low third of the grid is very low. As we saw today with Alex. So I think we need to improve the car and start a little bit higher up." The contact wasn't deemed worthy of investigation by the stewards, being a typical consequence of three cars fighting for the same patch of real estate at that corner. "It felt like there was a car on the right side of Fernando," explained Albon. "And he gave Fernando enough space as if he thought there was only one car on his inside. But then I was on the inside of Fernando. "So then I think it pinched and I tried to get out of the way and get on the kerb. But I didn't make good of it. So I imagine he got damage. I know I got damaged as we were driving around with a broken wing for the race." Read Also: How will Kimi Antonelli become F1 world champion at Mexico GP? item.title: Chargers vs. Rams Opening Odds: Bolts face challenge in Week 8
item.description: INGLEWOOD, CALIFORNIA - AUGUST 27: Derius Davis #12 of the Los Angeles Chargers tackled by Alex Johnson #36 of the Los Angeles Rams during the first half in a preseason game between the Los Angeles Rams and the Los Angeles Chargers at SoFi Stadium on August 27, 2026 in Inglewood, California. (Photo by Harry How/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Los Angeles Chargers are 0-6 after falling to the Kansas City Chiefs on the road in Week 6. Fresh off the bye, the Chargers will now face off against the crosstown rival Los Angeles Rams at SoFi Stadium. The Rams have found their fair share of struggles this season, but they are coming off of a Week 7 win against the Las Vegas Raiders, improving their record to 3-4. The Bolts entered this week as 7.5-point underdogs, per FanDuel Sportsbook . The over/under is currently set at 43.5 points. The Chargers struggled mightily against the Chiefs. The Chargers gave up a score on the opening drive and a touchdown the following possession, forcing them to play from behind all afternoon long. The offense was uninspiring, scoring just six points throughout the entire game. After the Miami Dolphins beat the New York Jets in Week 7, the Chargers are the only team in the league that has yet to win a game this season. That means they are in line for the No. 1 overall pick, but that wasn’t necessarily the goal going into the season. Perhaps the bye week will give the Chargers a chance to regroup and move forward as they try to grab their first win of the season to try and salvage something in 2026. BFTB community, how do you feel about the Chargers possibly getting their first win of the season against the Rams at SoFi Stadium in Week 8? Let us know in the comments section below.

(Photo by Ezra Shaw/Getty Images) Getty The Golden State Warriors dropped to 0-3 to start the season following Saturday’s loss to the Phoenix Suns. They were without seven players, including Steph Curry, Brandin Podziemski, Draymond Green and Al Horford, as the Warriors played the second game of a back-to-back. Ahead of Monday’s matchup against the Denver Nuggets, the Warriors received some pretty wonderful injury news. Steph Curry, Brandin Podziemski and More Cleared to Return Getty Stephen Curry #30 of the Golden State Warriors stands on the court during their preseason game against the Portland Trail Blazers at Chase Center on October 16, 2026 in San Francisco, California. According to the Golden State Warriors’ official injury report for Monday’s game against the Denver Nuggets, they will have a relatively healthy roster. Steph Curry, Brandin Podziemski, Draymond Green and Al Horford are not on the injury report. They are all available to play against a Nuggets team fresh off their first win of the season. Curry is being managed cautiously due to his right knee problem related to his patellofemoral pain syndrome diagnosis last season. Getty Brandin Podziemski #2 of the Golden State Warriors waits to shoot a free throw against the Los Angeles Lakers in the first quarter of a preseason game at T-Mobile Arena on October 13, 2026 in Las Vegas, Nevada. The Warriors defeated the Lakers 101-89. On the other hand, Podziemski is dealing with a lower back injury that has kept him out in two of the first three games of the season. He was one of the NBA’s iron men last season, appearing in all 82 games. As for Green and Horford, the Warriors are giving them extra rest throughout the season due to their age. Green is 36 years old, while Horford is one of only two players in the league aged 40 or older. Warriors vs. Nuggets Preview Getty Stephen Curry #30 of the Golden State Warriors and Nikola Jokic #15 of the Denver Nuggets go for a loose ball during the first half at Chase Center on October 23, 2025 in San Francisco, California. The Golden State Warriors are looking to earn their first win of the season when they take on the Denver Nuggets. They started the campaign with a 127-105 loss to the Los Angeles Lakers . The Warriors then followed it up with a close 111-108 defeat at the hands of the Memphis Grizzlies in their first home game of the season. And on Saturday, the short-handed Warriors gave the Phoenix Suns all they could handle. They came up short 131-122 , with rookie Yaxel Lendeborg scoring 26 points. Meanwhile, the Nuggets are coming off a 141-135 overtime win against the New Orleans Pelicans . They dropped the first game to the Oklahoma City Thunder and looked lackluster in the first three and a half quarters against the Pelicans. Rookie Trevon Brazile bailed out the Nuggets, with Jamal Murray and Nikola Jokic coming up clutch in overtime. item.title: Multiple Players Facing NFL Discipline Over Denver Broncos Game
item.description: Sean Payton could get bad news about Broncos starters Alex Singleton and Brandon Jones. Getty The Denver Broncos got the victory over the Arizona Cardinals in Week 7, but the NFL could double back for several players, including Alex Singleton and Brandon Jones. Singleton has run afoul of the NFL’s rules multiple times this season. He has already been fined for a late hit, a hit on a defenseless player (rescinded), and impermissible use of the helmet, and could add a second strike in any of those categories for his infraction against Arizona. It happened during the third quarter on a first-and-10 from the Broncos 30-yard line. Cardinals quarterback Jacoby Brissett’s pass intended for tight end Trey McBride fell incomplete, but officials flagged Singleton for “roughing the passer.” Singleton avoided costing the Broncos, as safety Brandon Jones was flagged for pass interference. The Cardinals chose to enforce Jones’ penalty over Singleton’s. However, per the NFL , Singleton’s infraction can cost players up to $17,911 for first offenses and $23,882 after that. Singleton has appealed two of his fines this season and could do the same for this one. That is, if one comes, since the NFL levies fines at its discretion and often docks players amounts that differ from what is listed on their official website. Unfortunately for head coach Sean Payton and the Broncos, Singleton is not the only player the NFL could have additional discipline for. Alex Singleton, Broncos Teammate Face Punishment From NFL Jones could also draw the NFL’s attention, and not for his PI during that outweighed Singleton’s roughing call in the Broncos’ win. During the first quarter on a first-and-10 from the Broncos 45-yard line, Cardinals running back Zonovan Knight took a handoff 29 yards. Broncos cornerback Jahdae Barron made the stop, but officials flagged Jones for “lowering the head to make forcible contact” in his failed attempt. Impermissible use of the helmet can incur fines as high as $23,882 for first-time infractions. Second offenses can incur $47,762 fines, but Jones also picks up his first strike. Three strikes in the same category triggers a one-game suspension. They can appeal those fines and decisions, and they could get some of their fine money back at the end of the season if they avoid further infractions. However, if the penalties stick, they will carry over into future seasons. Both players will look to play cleaner in Week 8 against the Kansas City Chiefs . NFL Could Take Look at Two Cardinals Players Jones and Singleton were the only Broncos players called for fineable offenses. However, two Cardinals could also hear from the NFL this coming week. The first call for a fineable offense of the game went against cornerback Kalen King. During a punt from Broncos punter Jeremy Crawshaw, officials flagged King for an “illegal blindside block.” That could see him draw a fine as high as $12, 537 for his first offense. item.title: Mbappé double secures Real Madrid late victory at Barcelona after Raphinha leveller
item.description: Thirteen years later, José Mourinho led Real Madrid into the Camp Nou as one team and them out again as another having secured the kind of late victory he loves and which opens up a whole new world. With just three minutes and the final reserves of energy remaining, a wonderful moment of skill from Jude Bellingham found Eduardo Camavinga and set them on one last run. Camavinga sprinted free, skilfully slipped Pau Cubarsí and pulled back for Kylian Mbappé to provide the finish, a little bit of history written. “The world that loves football will have stopped to watch this and they won’t have gone disappointed; this was two teams that played to win,” Mourinho said. It had been an intense, breathless ride, a proper battle, and it was his team who won it. Arriving right on time, Mbappé scored his second to make it 2-1, the Camp Nou falling quiet and their team given no time to react. They had drawn level after Mbappé’s opener, Raphinha scoring, but could not do it again. Continue reading...
